Question: What are some non-venomous snake species that can be dangerous to humans? Can these snakes be kept as pets?
Answer: The giant constrictor type of snakes can be dangerous to humans. The top two would probably be the African Rock Python and the Reticulated Python. Both Python varieties can grow to ridiculously large sizes, and are capable of easily asphyxiating humans, and in some cases, eating them up (at least smaller sized humans - even a huge Python would struggle to swallow up an Andre the Giant sized human). They have been kept as pets, but experts suggest that it is highly risky to keep these two varieties as pets. If you want to keep a Python as a pet, get a Ball Python. But I do know of people who keep these giant varieties as pets, and I always wonder why. Especially because the African Rock Python is one of the meanest snakes out there, and is likely to attack you right out of its eggshell (as a herpetologist sardonically said in an interview). But these are my top two picks for dangerous non-venomous snakes that should not be kept as pets.

Question: How dangerous are snake bites?
Answer: Snake bite is one of the most neglected diseases out there - each year about 5 million people are bitten, and about half of that happen to be envenoming i.e. not dry bites. From that number, about 600,000 people suffer either death or permanent disabilities including amputations. So, you can see that snake bites are indeed a huge danger. It does depend on where you’re getting bitten and by what snake. If you’re unlucky to get a bite from a sea snake for instance, and you’re far away from any medical facilities, then you’re going to die. Ditto if you happen to be in the middle of a remote jungle, and a venomous snake bites you and injects venom through the bite. If you’re too far away from medical assistance, then you are most likely looking at a one-way ticket to the pearly gates, or staring at necrosis of tissues and ensuing amputations. In India especially (the country with the highest incidences of reported snakebites and fatalities, thanks to the zealous efforts of the Big 4), the problem is further compounded, because of a severe lack of antivenin. The areas that are mostly in need of antivenin don’t have access to them, because they probably don’t have medical storage facilities, or no hospitals or clinics. Another huge problem in India is that India has one of the meanest snakes out there - the Russell’s Viper. That viper can really strike its entire body length - say, a snake is 5 feet long, and you’re 5 feet away, it can probably still launch itself at you to bite. And of course, you have the Saw Scaled Viper - another deadly one. The Kraits are even worse - you don’t even register their bite, since the bite is painless. A few hours later, you’re dead! The Cobra is another snake that is quite irritable and bites too - I personally think a Cobra bite is better than a Russel’s Viper bite, because the latter causes permanent damage to survivors. I suppose we should be grateful that India doesn’t have any spitting cobras (yet!) So, anyway, long answer to a short question - snake bites are damned deadly especially in countries and regions, where there isn’t an adequate supply of antivenin. India, Sri Lanka, many parts of Africa. Even in the US, if you’re unlucky to get bitten by a Coral Snake, you may be plumb out of luck. The antivenin for Coral Snakes is no longer manufactured - it’s just not profitable, so the company which made it doesn’t make it any more. But then again, if you look at just stats, I’m sure more humans kill snakes than the other way around. Still, it doesn’t take away from the fact that snakebite is a rather dangerous state of affairs, especially due to ever increasing encounters between humans and venomous snakes. The figure was taken from Joseph, N., Durairaj, S., Gowthaman, O., & Ganesan, V. K.’s 2022 article from Natural Resources for Human Health.

Question: Is Vladimir Putin an INTJ or an ISTP?
Answer: Vladimir Putin could be anything on the MBTI test. Depending on when he takes the test, and what his mood is like when he takes it, etc etc. On a sunny Wednesday, he could be an ESFJ…. but on a sultry Saturday, the man may well become an ESTP. One can hardly begin to predict what he’ll turn out to be on a maudlin Monday….perhaps an ISFP? If he took the test after putting away a lovely breakfast consisting of an Ossetra Caviar stuffed omelette along with lovely dark rye bread slathered with yellow butter, and then romps about with his pooch pals for a photoshoot in the snow…. he may well be an INFJ….. It all depends, you see…. Anyway, the reason for the flippancy above is that the MBTI is one of the biggest snake-oil tests out there. It’s not reliable, and nor is it valid. It’s not reliable because depending on where you’re taking it, when you’re taking it, and how you’re taking it, you will perhaps end up with different typologies. It’s not valid either because it is more or less akin to pseudoscience. Plenty of studies out there have debunked MBTI time and again - in fact, the only scientific source you will find that praises MBTI is a journal that is run by….(surprise!) The MBTI Foundation. Kind of like how Rand Paul is certified as a doctor by a board that is run by himself, his wife, and his father-in-law. Not very compelling, is it? But anyway, if you like playing around with the MBTI, one article touts that Putin is a ISTP, but some others mention he is an ISTJ. The title of the article is “Ukraine War: The 'Myers-Briggs Personality Types' of Putin, Zelensky & Biden. Are You Like Them?” But please do remember that the MBTI is not really useful in any major way.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is your review of the 2023 Indian movie, Bhoola starring Ajay Devgn?
Answer: Bholaa was good fun, and the movie jogs along well. It is the remake of Kaithi, and is almost identical but for a few different action scenes and a bit more backstory of the titular character (i.e. Ajay Devgn’s role). I thought Ajay did a good job of direction with this film - in his previous films , he did have the tendency to drag out the proceedings a tad bit much. Not so in Bholaa - the movie is tight and jogs along well. It is a taut action film and people who have not seen Kaithi will especially enjoy it. Even people who have seen Kaithi ought to like Bholaa - it offers enough of a change to keep the movie fun. Tabu is marvelous as always, and this I thought was an inspired bit of casting. A good decision to replace Bejoy with Diana, as it were. Kaithi did not have any meaty roles for any of the actresses in it, but Bholaa does thanks to Tabu. The villains are great here - Deepak Dobriyal and Vineet Kumar are both brilliant. Gajraj Rao is alright but I thought Stephen Raj was loads better in the original. Sanjay Mishra was just awesome too - he played the constable role with aplomb. And of course, Ajay Devgn was very good as the titular Bholaa. The child artistes were decent enough and so were the four youth who are stuck in the police building along with Sanjay Mishra. I really have nothing to complain about here - I also liked the extra breadth they’ve given here to set up the sequel. There is a neat cameo at the end that is fun, and another cameo that leaves you wanting more.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Do you have any reviews on Tu Jhoothi Main Makkar (Ranbir Kapoor and Shraddha Kapoor)?
Answer: I enjoyed the film for the most part. It pretty much follows the standard Luv Ranjan template. Comedy mixed with a dose of family and a dose of tragicomedy. And, critics will also get something to gripe about, in terms of their usual lament about Luv Ranjan’s misogyny. The performances of the various actors are decent, but Ranbir Kapoor steals the show throughout. His and Shraddha’s chemistry is hot and crackling, and I anticipate them to be cast together in more movies. The cameos of Nushrratt and Kartik Aaryan were a bit underwhelming though. Dimple Kapadia was splendid as Ranbir’s mother in the film. The rest of the cast was alright, but not spectacular. Even Boney Kapoor dons the actor’s hat in this film - he was decent enough too. The story buzzes along well, but does drag a little in the second half. On the whole though, it is a decent film to watch. Great music too, which the sparkling chemistry between Ranbir and Shraddha helps accentuate further. So, it is rather enjoyable fare for most! I’d give it a watch just to enjoy the smashing on-screen chemistry of Ranbir and Shraddha.

Question: What does Mr. Aamir Khan mean when he says "I am leaving"?

Question: What are the main criticisms of the film Great Grand Masti? Why did it receive such low ratings on IMDB and other sites?

That year saw the release of two other sex comedies(Mastizaade and Kya Kool Hain Hum 3), both of which performed poorly at the box office. I found Great Grand Masti to be a much better film than the other two. But there is no denying that there was a general feeling of exhaustion from the public, because of the glut of sex comedies. Too many sex comedies spoil the box office, I guess. The movie was fine for me, not as good as the previous two in the series, but nevertheless loads better than the other two sex comedies (Mastizaade and Kya Kool Hain Hum 3). While it wasn’t a great movie, it was not a lowly 3.7 score movie. I checked on the IMDB rating of its predecessor (Grand Masti), and that is a lowly 4.4. Balderdash to that low rating - the predecessor was a hilarious sex comedy, and one of my favorites. I guess sex comedy fans just don’t go on IMDB to vote, so only the humorless serious highfalutin folks go vote there. So for me at least, I don’t quite agree with the low IMDB scores of any of the Masti movies. Question: What are people's thoughts on Indian actors and actresses who marry foreigners? Is this criticized by other Indians or not really an issue? Why or why not?
Answer: There’s a critic for every possible situation or incident. We have seen loads of evidence for that, haven't we? So, that is true in this situation too. There are doubtless many people who criticize Indian actors or actresses who have foreign origin or foreign passport holding spouses. But I don’t think it’s an issue for most people. Most people don’t care about who other people marry, regardless of nationality. I mean - big deal, right! People should have the freedom to marry whoever they want, as long as the other person wants to marry them (i.e. provided it isn’t some sort of forced or coerced arrangement). Many Indian actors and actresses have foreign spouses - some are divorced now, but they did have a foreign spouse for a lengthy amount of time. I don’t recall ever meeting anyone who has had any harsh criticisms to make of those people. I mean I’m sure there are some out there, but I have never crossed paths with any such types. So, from my perspective, it’s a non-issue. It would only ever become an issue if the actor suddenly decides to become a politician or some such. Then, the foreignness of the spouse can become sorta an albatross around their neck.

Question: Can you name some actresses who you think would be good as an Indian mom or housewife? Why do you think they would be good in those roles?

Most movies: if the lead actress is a younger mom, typically it’s not the main focus of the film. But sometimes it is - so, it does depend! All the ones in the collage up there have done well in mom roles, be it in fleeting peripheral roles or main plot roles. So, I’ll say that any actress can play a convincing mom role - unless of course, she ends up playing a mom to someone who is her senior many times over. Imagine how dumb it would be if Disha Patani were to play the mother of Salman Khan in some movie - that would be ludicrous, wouldn’t it? The only time I can sort of see that being okay was in Paa, when Vidya Balan played the mother of Amitabh Bachchan.

Question: Who was the first actress to play an IPS officer on screen in Bollywood movies?

The next one who portrayed an IPS officer role is probably Tabu in Drishyam, and then it would be Priyanka Chopra in Jai Gangaajal. I think Yami Gautam is playing one now in Dasvi. There are many more I’m sure, but these are the ones who play IPS officer roles which are identifiable (for the most part) on screen.

Question: Which of the following actors has played a cop role, and how good were they: Amitabh Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan, Aamir Khan or Salman Khan?

In terms of how good they were, I would say that Amitabh was probably the best. Salman has been fairly good in all his cop roles, while Aamir was excellent in the three films he has done a cop role in. Shah Rukh Khan only did a cop role in one movie, and so it wouldn’t be fair to compare him with the rest. He ought to do at least a couple more as a cop - dunno why he’s never done as many as his contemporary actors.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Did Jhanvi Kapoor ever leave the film industry to enter Bollywood?
Answer: Yes indeed, I often leave a restaurant in order to go to a restaurant. As the wonderful collage below demonstrates Janhvi Kapoor has often left something in order to enter the same thing. For instance, she has left the water in order to enter the water. She has also left the gym in order to enter the gym. She has left a car in order to enter a car etcetera etc. Time is nonlinear after all, as so many cultures believe. When do we leave, and when do we enter? Who can tell with a modicum of certainty? This is a wonderful thought provoking philosophical query by our darling QPG! Can we truly enter someplace if we never leave it? Or do we have to leave someplace if we wish to enter it? Deep, very deep! I’m not a philosopher, but if I was, I could surely rustle up a thought-provoking response to this brilliant QPG question. But alas, all I can do is literally take the question at face value. Oh well…

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Alia Bhatt married to Ranbir Kapoor's brother Karan Kapoor? Do they look similar in appearance?
Answer: Absolutely, darling QPG, you have uncovered one of the biggest secrets of all time. Indeed, there is a hidden secretive sibling involved here. But it’s not Karan Kapoor; you are thinking of Thalia Bhatt, who is the secretive twin sister of Alia Bhatt. Mahesh Bhatt named Alia’s twin as Thalia, but then he realized that sadly most folks would think of Thalia as referring to claps and not the intended homage to the amazing Mexican pop star Thalia. Mahesh Bhatt already the most reviled man in Bollywood, could not bear to have this new scorn and ridicule heaped on his frail shoulders. He shuddered thinking of critics alleging how desperate Mahesh was for claps and praise that he named his daughter Thalia. So, the secret had to be buried, and it remained buried up until today, when the daring QPG had laid it bare for the entire world. Poor Mahesh Bhatt - always craving Thalia but only getting Gaaliyan. Sigh… The above is of course nonsensical QPG inspired creative writing - Ranbir does not have a brother called Karan (has an uncle though, I think!), and Alia has not married Karan Kapoor. Alia has married Ranbir, and if they have siblings named Thalia and Karan, they only exist in the minds of the QPG (and mine, I guess, since I invented one of them).

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why do Indian actresses do adult scenes in family movies? Don't they know that children are watching them expose their midriff and navel when they shouldn't be?
Answer: Thankfully most Indians are not Talibanesque in their views, and don’t have this ardent burning desire to cover every inch of a woman’s body, with an opaque tarpaulin. And, zero family movies have adult scenes - if they have adult scenes, they are not going to be classified as family flicks. I don’t remember any “adult scenes” in movies like Taare Zameen Par or Stanley Ka Dabba or any other such family type movie. If you’re confusing movies like the Murder series or the Jism or the Raaz series with family flicks, then that’s a categorization problem. Some movies are not really meant for children‘s consumption; so, just exercise judicious discretion while selecting movies to watch with your family. But I do take exception at your point about midriffs and navels - big bloody deal! That’s not even adult in any way, as per me! Swimwear in an oceanic or beach setting isn’t adult or indecent either. Except for Talibanesque dolts, maybe. While yes, children should probably not be watching any adult movies, I don’t consider them seeing an actress’ mid-riff or navel any cause for concern. You may find it titillating, but that’s your issue. Children are unlikely to do so - I think there’s no real need to overreact. Blaming an actress is not pertinent - if you think you need to protect your kids from ever witnessing a woman’s midriff or navel, then don’t show them anything except Barjatya movies.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What was the reason behind Anushka Sharma's character being a doctor in her movie Pari?
Answer: The reason is not very hard to imagine, darling QPG. After all, Pari roughly translates to Fairy. And, since nurses have claimed the Angel tag, doctors are pretty much left with only the fairy tag. So, as we all know, in Pari, Anushka’s character is a self-made doctor who studies YouTube videos from Salman Khan’s Being Human academy, which is used by students all over the globe to crack IIT, IIM, IAS, MIT, BMC, FBI, CIA, etc etc exams. The movie never does explain though how she has good internet facilities in her hut; because the hut seems to be next to a stream in a jungle of sorts. Unelectrified even! But I suppose that’s the joy of Jio - bloody Airtel couldn’t have done it, that’s for sure! Anyway, so then Anushka’s character becomes a doctor, to prove to the world and naysayers that she too can become a doctor. Almost like a Pari Behen MBBS of sorts! This brought tears to the eyes of even the visually challenged amongst us. And her turn from slovenly wild child to a posh and glamorous doctor was marvelous. Of course, those of us who live in this colorless humdrum of an existence we have, know that nothing written above is true. Only the dear QPG can come up with fantastic plots like above. In reality, Pari is a horror movie, and she was not a doctor in it. She plays a fairy of sorts, not like Tinkerbelle but a more dangerous sort. It’s a good movie, but kinda sad - if the QPG plot premise had been true, it would have been an entirely different movie altogether.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Did Aamir Khan wear a hijab in his movie Dangal?
Answer: What a fantastic question this is - but sadly, the answer is much more pedestrian than the question deserves. No, Aamir Khan was not donning a Hijab in Dangal - after all, since he was playing the role of the Poghat Patriarch, Mahavir Singh Poghat (a decidedly Hindu character), a hijab (regardless of how beautiful it may be) did not quite fit the character’s portrayal. He has appeared in drag a few times in ads and movies, but even then, never in a hijab. He does have pictures next to women with hijabs, but look closely, with your beady-eyed code, QPG, Aamir Khan isn’t the one wearing a hijab. Poor Aamir Khan gets criticized if he even takes a picture with a woman in a hijab, imagine the resultant furor if he were to be wearing a hijab himself.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Who was approached to play Kattappa's wife in 'Baahubali' series, and why were they rejected?
Answer: By golly! There was intense competition among several beautiful starlets and divas, as they were all vying with one another to bag the role of Katappa’s wife. After all, the Katappa role was the most glamorous of all, wasn’t it, darling QPG? You had internationally renowned actresses like Scarlett Johansson and Monica Bellucci competing with homegrown Indian talent like Disha Patani and AFAIK even Salma Hayek threw her hat into the ring, to get to be cast as Mrs. Katappa. But alas, twas not meant to be. Baahubali & Bijjaladeva’s baes were furious at the prospect of their glamor being affected by these international beauties. So they forced the hapless director to change the entire script. Instead of Katappa being the gregarious chick-magnet he was, they changed him into a slave of the Queen. And sadly, there was resultantly, no scope for anyone to play his reel life wife. Sigh! Katappa fans have yet to recover from the shock and trauma. Lest anyone reads the above and comes away thinking that yours truly has gone cuckoo - I would ask them to take a deep breath and do some pranayama yoga. The QPG’s ridiculous fictional questions deserve ridiculous fictional answers, don’t they?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the name of the Bollywood actress with the most heart-breaking life outside of films?
Answer: There are several Bollywood actresses who have had miserable real lives, in stark contrast to their reel-life images. However, the one actress who stands out, at least in my mind is Madhubala. She was divinely and exquisitely beautiful, and blessed with a wonderful screen presence. However, her real life was plagued with a variety of tragedies. She grew up in a poor household, and ended up having to support her family with her earnings. They in turn were interfering to the hilt, and caused her to have to choose between them and her romantic partner. Then it turned out that she had a congenital heart defect, which struck her down at a relatively young age (i.e. 36). Meena Kumari is also an actress who fits this question - she had similar tragic circumstances in her life. I guess anytime there are overly interfering and dependent family members in an actress’s life, things turn out tragic for them. You see this happen all over the globe, and that too especially for families of child artistes, regardless of if they go on to become actors as adults or not.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How is Ranbir Kapoor dealing with his breakup from Alia Bhatt?
Answer: As far as I can tell, Ranbir Kapoor is taking this calamitous news very seriously. He has grown a rough and tough beard, and appears to be smoking too. Rather Animal like in his appearance, with all the blood on his shirt, and the bloody axe - I just don’t know what to say here. Oh wait a tick - that’s just his character’s appearance for his upcoming movie Animal. Judging from the image and the director attached, Ranbir’s character will most probably be a ramped up Arjun Reddy/Kabir Singh type character. It does appear that he’s on his way to the code parents of the QPG to give them a piece of his mind in this getup, for making the QPG spit out these sort of garbage fictitious questions. In reality, of course, he and Alia Bhatt have not broken up, and are still happily married. They even had a baby recently - so, no dice here, QPG!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Are Hrithik Roshan and Pooja Hegde currently in a relationship?
Answer: Ah, the possibilities were infinite. What a smashing pair this combo could have been. Hrithik with Pooja would be a sight for sore eyes, and the lovely pair never failed to bring even the most cynical of souls into a state of dewy eyes. Such is the power of a gentle yet robust loving relationship, isn’t it? But alas, ‘twas not meant to be. A verdant green with jealousy reptile did all he could to break up the happy couple, even going so far as to soar above the water, like some sort of crocodilian Michael Phelps. The above is of course a condensed version of the plot of the insanely boring and dreary Mohenjo Daro, which starred Hrithik and Pooja Hegde. Honestly, I am still a bit hazy about the movie’s plot. All I can recall from the film is the memorable crocodile shooting out from the water scene. When the only thing you can recall from a movie is the creature, and the movie isn’t a creature feature, then we know that it’s time to go back to the drawing board. Sorta like going to a Biryani place and only fondly remembering the Paan there. But anyway, back to this puzzling query from our dear QPG - no, Hrithik Roshan and Pooja Hegde are not in a relationship, not currently and not previously either! They’ve barely interacted with each other except for that one dreary flick where they acted together!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the reason for BJP leaders threatening to stop the release of Baahubali 2?
Answer: One could engage in idle speculation, and hypothesize some possible solutions. One is that the BJP leaders got confused and upset when they found out that everyone would know why Katappa betrayed Baahubali. As diehard Katappa fans, they obviously did not want any mud to be smeared on their hero. Another possible reason is that they found out that the darling “Milky Beauty” Tamannaah barely has any role in the sequel. These are valid reasons to threaten to stop the release of Baahubali 2. All moot though because the movie released several years ago. And of course, there is the alternative solution that this never happened. In reality, no BJP leader, in fact nobody at all, advocated for a boycott of Baahubali 2. This is yet another fail from the QPG factory of churned out fictitious questions. I’m guessing it conjured up this ridiculous question because of headlines like these “Baahubali director criticizes BJP leader for his Besharam Rang position” or some such. Too much of a reach this, my dear QPG!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What did Kareena Kapoor do in Bareilly Ki Barfi?
Answer: Kareena Kapoor is an inveterate foodie. She loves eating a variety of awesome dishes, and does seem to enjoy the pleasures of deliciousness. This includes dishes as varied as Paya, Pizza, Biryani, Croissants, Ice Cream, Halwa, Strawberries & Cream, Sarson Ka Saag and Makke ki Roti, etc etc. She does make sure to work it out too, so it’s not like it’s interfering with her keeping fit. I would imagine that that’s what Kareena Kapoor did during Bareilly Ki Barfi. While I am not sure if Kareena Kapoor indulged in platefuls of Barfis during Bareilly Ki Barfi, she must have for sure enjoyed some of her other favorite meals. After all, there is not even a single shot of her in Bareilly Ki Barfi. Hmm…come to think of it, she may not be in the movie at all. No wonder, one never got to see her in the movie at all. Yes, that must be the simple solution - she simply isn’t in the movie! So, elementary, my dear QPG - she did nothing at all in Bareilly Ki Barfi.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Do you think Kareena Kapoor will be a good mother, since she doesn't have much knowledge about children or family life in general (she's from film industry)?
Answer: Well, darling QPG, what we think here hardly matters since Kareena is already a mother, and of two children, at that. One is Taimur and the other is Jehangir. Both kids appear to be well-loved, and seem to be doing alright. So, she seems to be doing fine as a mother. I do wonder though about the latter part of your question. Yes, she is from the “film industry”. But no, that does not mean that people from the film industry have absolutely zilch knowledge about children or family life. They’re not all gibbering idiots who lack all kinds of sense. People from all walks of life can be equally good or bad when it comes to being parents or spouses. One cannot simply generalize and say that people are going to be bad at family life because they’re from the film industry. I mean to say, prior to joining the film industry, most would have had families themselves, be it growing up in one, or having access to one. It’s not like they were generated via means of computer code, and made to mimic human intelligence, is it?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Who is more famous, Mahesh Bhatt or Mukesh Bhatt? Why so? What's their contribution to Hindi cinema industry as producers and directors respectively?
Answer: The question of fame It has to be Mahesh Bhatt - even people who don’t watch his or any movies know about him. Mahesh Bhatt is both famous as well as infamous - he’s always had the habit of speaking his mind, and isn’t in the slightest bit shy about expressing his views and opinions, no matter however off or controversial they may be. Also, everyone will recall how he was lynched in the conspiratorial Covid-time Kangaroo court of public opinion. Accused of having orchestrated Sushant Singh Rajput’s murder, and of having driven to his residence and done so personally, etc etc. Mukesh on the other hand is much less recognizable, and not many people will be able to identify Mukesh Bhatt in a lineup. The question of contributions As far as their contributions to cinema - they have both done their bits. Mukesh more as a producer and Mahesh more as a director. Mahesh Bhatt was a well regarded movie director, and has made some fine movies through the years. Mukesh has produced many of those films. So, it’s hard to compare them on an even level, since their work roles have been different.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Are Shraddha Kapoor and Ranbir Kapoor getting married soon after their film "Tujhse Fraaandship Karoge"?
Answer: I sincerely hope that there will never be a movie called “Tujhse Fraandship Karoge”. In fact, I am tempted to go and register the title myself so nobody will ever make a movie with that dismal title. Secondly, they’re coming in a movie called “Tu Jhooti Main Makkar”, not that hideous title in the question. Anyway, this was yet another delightful rib-tickler from the QPG! I guess the QPG is learning all this from the QPP type questions which used to exist earlier. Oh well!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Do you think Ranveer Singh did a good job as Vijay Deenanath Chauhan in Bajirao Mastani? Why or why not?
Answer: He did a fantastic job as Vijay Deenanath Chauhan in Bajirao Mastani. A tad bit incongruous to see that, but it’s alright. It was at least less anachronistic than it was when we saw Sunny Leone’s character from Mastizaade in the biopic of Mother Teresa, and let’s not even mention the time that Vijay Raaz’s character from Run appeared as the titular role in the Mike Tyson biopic. What’s that you say - that hasn’t happened? Well neither has Ranveer Singh ever essayed the Agneepath character role, and that too in a period flick. Ah, these wonderful flights of fancy! Nobody can out-troll with nonsensical questions like the good old QPG! I salute your codeparents, QPG! I wonder how the POE will reply to queries like these.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What does Shah Rukh Khan think of his ex-wife Gauri's new relationship with Bollywood actor Sanjay Dutt?
Answer: Shah Rukh Khan does not even spend a single solitary moment thinking about this absurd proposition. That is because what you suggest, darling QPG, is complete asinine nonsense. Gauri Khan is not Shah Rukh Khan’s ex-wife; they are still happily married to each other. Poor Sanjay Dutt is also happily married to Maanyata. It is quite dumb to link him with Gauri Khan. Anyway, another fail here - this question is completely incorrect on so many levels. You’ll certainly need to evolve significantly, dear QPG - right now, most of your questions read like the rotten ones at the height of the QPP fervor.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the role of Bollywood in the popularity of fairness creams among Indians?
Answer: While Bollywood certainly deserves its fair share of blame - it does not deserve all of the blame. Bollywood did not establish India’s societal culture. It has ability to influence it but cannot claim to be establishing it. Does anyone really think that if Shah Rukh Khan or Yami Gautam or any other actor/actress stops advertising fair and lovely type products, that people’s attitudes towards fair skin will change? Newsflash - they undoubtedly won’t! “Fair good, dark bad” is a horrible cultural sentiment that is prevalent globally. Anthropologists and sociologists can probably come up with a seasoned explanation as to why that is so. For India, I guess Turkic and British colonization through the ages influenced this stupid obsession with fair skin. So all Bollywood does is show a mirror on what Indian culture is! They do their part surely in getting people to buy those dumb bleaching lotions, but even if they didn’t, people would still buy those toxic lotions.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What was the reason for the outrage against Deepika Padukone for wearing an orange dress at Cannes?
Answer: Was there any outrage? This is the first time I’m reading about any outrage against Deepika Padukone for wearing an orange dress at Cannes. The only old article I found mentioned that she was trolled because the train of her orange dress was a bit cumbersome, and looked slightly uncomfortable. Trolling does not equate to outrage! I think her red outfit was deemed more comfortable, but who really knows, right? Anyway, there was no outrage, at least not a broad widespread form of it. One or two dudes may have gotten “outraged” because people like that love getting outraged. But really, not a big deal, is it?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why did Deepika Padukone turn into a vulgar actress?
Answer: I suppose this question sprang up in your mind, after you saw the video of the song Besharam Rang from Pathaan. Yes, she is gyrating in the song in a rather glamorous avatar, but what of it? The movie is a slick action flick filled to the brim with glamor, after all. One can hardly expect Deepika Padukone to be donning a ghoonghat or burkha or nun’s habit in the song, can one? I disagree with your insinuation - she has not turned into a vulgar actress. There is nothing vulgar about wearing a bikini or beachwear. By the way, Shah Rukh Khan is sans his shirt throughout the song - is he now a vulgar actor? This whole notion of vulgarity is an entirely subjective matter. Typically, orthodox fuddy-duddies are never happy unless a woman is completely covered with a burlap sack. Don’t be like them!

Name: Aditya Simha

Answer: Arbaaz Khan is on his way right now to Quora’s HQ to insist on a meeting with the QPG developers. Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How does Ranveer Singh feel about Deepika Padukone's marriage with Ranbir Kapoor?
Answer: Ranveer Singh is shocked, shocked, I tell you! His poor sensitive mind is completely frazzled, and the thin line that separates insanity from genius has been forcibly and resolutely erased. Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How tall is Deepika Padukone? What are her vital stats like weight, cup size, etc.? How does it compare with other Bollywood actresses like Priyanka Chopra and Katrina Kaif?
Answer: Darling QPG, I can see that you are most desirous of obtaining these riveting bits of information. As far as Deepika Padukone is concerned, I believe she is 5 feet 8 inches tall. I have no clue about her actual weight, although she can’t weigh very much. Her cup size when compared with Priyanka Chopra and Katrina Kaif is a completely different matter altogether. Anyway, if I had to guess, I would say that Deepika’s cup is probably sized at 6 ounces. Katrina Kaif’s is definitely 14 ounces or so - she must be hardly sleeping a wink after sipping so much caffeine. Priyanka’s cup size is somewhere in the middle - I’d say, maybe 8 ounces? Couldn’t be sure though! Anyway, hope this lovely answer about their respective cup sizes provides you with lots of clarity. I do believe they are all coffee drinkers, but could possibly use their cups for tea too. Can’t say for sure! P.S - What a wonderful question, QPG! This is straight out of the books of the most resilient cave dwellers from the recent past.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Who is the Indian actress who had no formal training in acting but turned out to be a very good actress nonetheless?
Answer: As far as I can tell, Tabu has never been to any formal school in acting. Nor has she ever flown to New York University or the University of South California to “attend” or “study” in acting workshops like so many of today’s actors and actresses tend to do. Instead, she started off in somewhat weaker movies, but has now attained a stature, where she is almost always the USP of the film. Check out any of her performances in the recent past - all mind blowing and brilliant! Even if the rest of the cast and the plot is weak, Tabu always stands strong and tall above the mediocrity of the movie. She is absolutely and without any doubt breathtaking in her magnificence. Tabu is the best actress pan-India! In my view, no other actress comes close to Tabu’s prowess!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Do you think Poonam Pandey's tweets are in good taste?
Answer: This is a rather odd question, dear QPG! Poonam Pandey is not really known for her outlandish tweets! Yes, if this were a question about her penchant for scandalous attire or the lack thereof, then one could examine the question of whether they are in good taste or not. Fearmongers, pedophiles, unholy terrorists, populist idiots, etc etc. Poonam Pandey’s tweets are at most a trifle bit gossipy perhaps or a bit naughty; no real harm in them. The real harmful, and the extremely in poor taste tweets are delivered by fearmongers and idiot twits who are running rampant on Twitter. Poonam Pandey is practically as pure as the driven snow in comparison.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Could I beat Gal Gadot in a fight? I'm a 16-year-old boy, 6'0 & 150 lbs, skinny & untrained.
Answer: No, you could not! You must have seen those pictures of Gal Gadot being accompanied by several shorter dudes, right? Well, those guys are not minions as internet memes would have you believe. They are bodyguards who will whip the bejeezus out of you or anyone else who they perceive as a threat to their client. Also, why do you want to fight Gal Gadot anyway? When I was 16 (and even today ), the last thing I wanted to do is to fight with a beautiful actress. What the hell kind of fantasy is that? If you must indulge in fighting, go join some mixed gender MMA club, and live out your heart’s desire. If you meet Gal somewhere, say a hello to her, and get a selfie or something. Much better to do that than to desire to fight her.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Who is a better actor: Imran Khan or Ranbir Kapoor? Why should we choose one over another? Who has more potential to become a star in future than the other one?
Answer: Darling QPG, this question is hopelessly outdated. Imran Khan has already pretty much retired from movies. The last movie he appeared in was in 2015, in Katti Batti. Practically impossible to expect him to come back now like a Phoenix, and resurrect the ashes of his career. At the most, he can come back as a character actor or a director or something. Ranbir Kapoor on the other hand is not only a bigger star than Imran Khan, he is also a much better actor. I liked Imran Khan but in comparison with Ranbir Kapoor, he stands no chance. Ranbir Kapoor is a gifted actor, and really accomplished. Imran was alright, but not the greatest. He was good in rom-coms, but not really good in anything that was in a different genre. I do think though that he was unfairly blamed for the turkey Once Upon ay Time in Mumbai Dobaara. That was a shit movie but it wasn’t shit only because of Imran Khan. Its stupid title misspelling didn’t work, did it Ekta Kapoor? But anyway, in any prowess comparison between Ranbir and Imran - the former easily trounces the latter. Imran is sadly consigned to the history books now - I do not see a way for him to become a star again.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: In which film did Shah Rukh Khan play a blind man?
Answer: I don’t think he’s played a blind man in any of his movies. Usually, Bollywood actors don’t play disabled character roles (with the exception of Hrithik Roshan, who’s played at least two different ones). The closest Shah Rukh Khan has come to playing a blind man is in Baadshah, where he pretends to be a blind man for a bit, in order to fool Twinkle Khanna’s character. And, I suppose one could make a case that he’s myopically blind in Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, because he miraculously only romantically notices Kajol after she sheds her tomboy avatar, and dons a glamorous one. But otherwise, he has not played any blind man roles. If I were him, I wouldn’t be running about trying to play one either. The movie will flop badly if he plays a blind man. Bollywood audiences aren’t really that keen to watch their main leads play disabled character roles. Sad, but true! Apart from Kaabil and Barfi, I can’t think of too many films with disabled main lead characters, that were successful.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Do Indian actors refuse to work with Pakistani actresses? If so, why?
Answer: They generally didn’t used to, especially prior to 2016. Many actors have appeared opposite Pakistani actresses. This list includes pairs such as Shah Rukh Khan & Mahira Khan, Mithun Chakraborty & Salma Agha , Saif Ali Khan & Somy Ali, Ashmit Patel & Meera, Himesh Reshammiya & Sara Loren, Harshwardhan Rane & Mawra Hocane, and Irrfan Khan & Saba Qamar, etc etc etc. But then the Uri terror attack happened in 2016, and Pakistani actors were banned in Bollywood movies. Then the 2019 Pulwama terror attack happened, and the All Indian Cine Workers Association announced a total ban on all Pakistani actors and artists. As of today, the ban is still in effect - so, even if Indian actors would want to work with Pakistani actresses, they would probably not be able to do so, unless the ban is lifted. And, till the ban is lifted, Indian movie producers aren’t going to be very keen on casting Pakistani actresses in their films.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is your review of the 2022 Indian Billingual movie, Godfather starring Chiranjeevi and Salman Khan?
Answer: I saw this movie in a theater last evening, and I must say that I rather enjoyed it. Yes indeed, the movie is a remake, but so what, it was a good remake. The original may be better and all that, but this remake isn’t bad at all. The performances are all top-notch, with one small exception. Chiranjeevi is excellent as Brahma, Nayanthara is also fabulous as Satya, Satyadev is fantastic as Jai, and Murali Sharma steals every scene he’s in. Sunil turns in a really decent performance, and one that you do not anticipate at all - I also liked Bhramaji in his role. And, I really loved Salman’s cameo in the movie. He’s looking fit and dapper, and seemed to be having fun in his role, which is the only way to see Salman at his best. The only performance I thought wasn’t quite up to muster was the performance of Puri Jagannadh - an actor like Vennela Kishore would have been much better instead. But Puri Jagganadh isn’t really an actor, so we can give him some credit. He did his best, but acting is not his forte - but after Liger I suppose he is in dire straits, so it’s good that he’s exploring acting opportunities. The item song (Blast Baby) in the end juxtaposed with a lot of fighting was crude to the hilt - it could have been entirely done away with. I would have liked to have seen a mano-y-mano fight between Salman/Chiru and Nawab Shah, but alas, that was not to be. Anyway, the movie is basically Lucifer packaged with more crowd pleasing script changes, as Tollywood audiences demand. I enjoyed it, and I think most will enjoy it - it is after all a million times better than the atrocious Acharya.

Question: How many Indian actresses wear hijabs on screen and off screen in Bollywood? Why do they choose to cover their heads with the scarf while acting or otherwise?

Most other Bollywood actresses though, be they Muslim or otherwise, are usually not so conservatively inclined. Question: Why don’t some Indians like Dhadkan, a romantic Hindi movie, while mostly people like this movie madly?

Although, I suspect that I liked the movie more because I like Akshay and Suniel, than anything else. So, my guess is the people who disliked the movie did so due to a combination of the following reasons - (i) They hate the romantic Film genre, (ii) They hate Akshay and/or Suniel, (iii) They disliked the mellifluous music, (iv) They dislike all Bollywood movies by principle alone, and (v) They went to the movie expecting an action fest, and got a romantic melodrama. And, of course, there could be a multitude of many other reasons and rationales. But the bottom line is that it isn’t too much of a mystery as to why some people disliked the movie, while others liked it.

Question: How 'Disha Patani' is pronounced?
Answer: Disha Patani has a name that is prone to having a lot of people pronounce it incorrectly. Disha itself is an easy name to get right - after all there are loads of names that rhyme with it. For instance, some other names that rhyme with Disha are Misha, Prisha, Nisha, and Trisha. Patani however is a bit trickier - when you read it in English, it is tempting to pronounce it as Puh-Ta-nee, but the real pronunciation is more like Paat-nee. So her name is pronounced as Di-Sha Paat-nee. As, I said, It’s a lot easier to recognize and understand the pronunciation when you see her name in Hindi. Question: What is your comment on Kamaal R. Khan's arrest by the Mumbai police?

Does Rahul Kanal intend to make similar complaints about many of his fellow Shiv Sainiks, who have run off their mouths in public forums and social media? So, my comment on this matter is that unfortunately it looks like Freedom of Speech is going to go for a toss now. People will start filing cases against whoever they feel has aggrieved them or others on social media. Freedom of speech means that one has to tolerate the occasional troll like KRK. Also, aren’t there any real criminals that the Mumbai Police could perhaps go and arrest instead? KRK’s destructive tweeting isn’t that dangerous in reality - after all, one day, he will meet a better and bigger troll than him, who will trounce him convincingly.

Question: Why do people hate M. Night Shyamalan so much? What makes him such a bad director in your opinion?
Answer: I think the biggest reason why people dislike (hate seems a bit much here) M. Night Shyamalan is that they expect a stunning plot twist in every one of his movies. And when the plot twist comes, they usually don’t like it, or they bemoan that the twist was too easy to guess. M.N.S’ first three big budget movies were great - Sixth Sense, Unbreakable, and Signs are all great flicks, and fun to watch even today. Then came the massive stinker, The Village. That movie had a horrid plot twist, which spoiled the entire movie. Then came Lady in the Water, The Happening, The Last Airbender, and (oh boy!) After Earth. Four stinkers in a row, and three with dumb plot twists, which would have been easy to spot, a mile away, by a deaf, mute, and blind viewer. My guess is that these four flops perhaps really destroyed his reputation. Since then, he’s improved a bit, or at least, tried to go back, somewhat, to the good old times of his initial trio of successes. I quite enjoyed The Visit, Split, and Glass, but found that Old had a ludicrous plot twist of its own. So anyway, I don’t think he’s a bad director - just that sometimes his direction is rather predictable. When it’s not, when the twist works, his direction isn’t to be faulted. It’s only when the twist fails, when his direction gets hauled over the coals. So, I would argue that his directorial abilities are proportional to his script writing prowess. When his story or script is weak, then the resultant movie seems like it is poorly directed. Anyway, in recent times, I really enjoyed The Visit. It had a fabulous twist, and is a rather good movie.

Question: Did the Western critics and audience really like the RRR movie or is it just some well coordinated PR stunt by Netflix?
