Question: Ranbir Kapoor went to Kangana Ranaut's home to offer a role in Sanju, but why did she reject it?
Answer: She would have most certainly accepted the role if Hrithik would also have joined Ranbir, in order to beseech her to accept a role in Sanju. Alas, that was not the case. What’s that you say? Why would Hrithik go to Kangana to beg her to act in Sanju? Well, it’s about as equally plausible as is her tale of Ranbir going to her house to offer her a role in Sanju. I find it a bit tough to believe that Ranbir goes about offering roles in movies where he’s not even the producer. I would have been more inclined to believe this if she had claimed that Vidhu Vinod Chopra had offered her a role in Sanju. That would have been perfectly understandable - but then Vidhu is infamous for being an irate sort of chap, and may have reacted poorly to stories like that. Much easier to choose Ranbir Kapoor, who is rather more likely to let stories like that go around without commenting on their veracity.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How is the Bollywood mafia sabotaging the acting career of Kim Sharma?
Answer: They are doing no such thing. Her decision to quit cinema has nothing to do with some imaginary Bollywood mafia conspiracy. Kim’s films didn’t work - that’s it! After her initial debut success, all of her other movies met a rather dismal fate at the box office. And then she voluntarily left what she called a non-existent career. While it is tempting to blame a “Bollywood mafia” for one’s lack of success, the reality is that if an actor has a lot of successful movies, then nothing can stop them from having a good career. If Kim had a couple more hits after her debut film, she’d have had a lengthier career. Sadly for her, that was not to be the case. Anyway, she seems to be happy with Leander Paes now - so, let’s wish her all the best.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why did Sahil Khan leave Bollywood?
Answer: It is not that a big a mystery as to why Sahil Khan chose to leave his film career. The only successful movie of his was Style, and it wasn’t a half-bad movie, but the acting honors in that movie went to Sharman Joshi. All of Sahil’s other movies were huge bombs, and the worst of the lot was his last movie Ramaa : The Savior. That pretty much turned out to be the final nail in his film career’s coffin. He may obliquely hint now that Salman Khan ruined his career and all of that, but the truth of the matter is that if his other films had worked, he would have continued on as an actor in films. One does not voluntarily choose to leave a movie industry, and I don’t think Sahil did either. A lack of good offers is what he faced. He seems to be doing fine as a fitness entrepreneur, YouTuber, and Instagrammer. He is not a movie star, but still retains some level of celebrity status. Check out his various pics - literally all his pics are him with bikini babes. He’s doing excellent by that metric, and that possibly fuels his success as a fitness entrepreneur.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How is Kiara Advani getting so many movies?
Answer: Kiara has the Oomph factor in plenty - she looks amazing on screen, and has a brilliant relatability. Every single time I see her on screen, she looks delightful. And, she has the excellent ability to look at ease in both glamorous as well as girl next door roles. She also looks great opposite anyone she costars with. Additionally, she has some powerful godparents - for e.g., Salman is a friend of Kiara’s aunt, KJo has taken a real shine to her, and even Akshay is sort of like a mentor of hers. It is therefore hardly surprising that she is getting loads of movie roles. She looks the part, and has powerful backers - what could be better than that?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: After a 1955 Devdas (Dilipkumar, Suchitra Sen, Vaijayantimala) and a 2002 Devdas (Sharukh Khan, Aishwarya Rai, Madhuri Dixit) whom do you want to see in lead roles of a 2023 Devdas movie?
Answer: I actually have no desire to watch a Devdas movie, be it in 2023 or later. The 2002 version was pretty near damned un-watchable for me. Shah Rukh Khan hammed it up like nobody’s business. Anyway, that movie was too maudlin for me, like most (not all) of Bhansali’s movies usually are. So, I really don’t want to see anyone make or ever remake another Devdas again. The 1955 version was better than the 2002 version, but again, I'm not inordinately desirous to watch this maudlin tragedy again. Unrequited love does not need to become a self imposed death sentence. There are other classic stories that would make better movie material. Perhaps, our film producers and directors should start delving into other stories, rather than incessantly making and remaking the same stuff over and over. Everyone and their uncle knows the story of Devdas - time to move on.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why does Disha Patani always wear bikinis?
Answer: She does not always wear bikinis - but she does when she’s doing ad campaigns or on a beach or the ocean or some such place. It is disingenuous to claim that she is always wearing bikinis. You may feel like that because you only seek out images of her in bikinis. But take a deeper dive into her profile, and you’ll find plenty of non-bikini images. Yes, you’ll find plenty of bikini images too, but what of it? She looks great in them, and is super comfortable with them.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why is Malaika Arora so loose in character that she is now dating Arjun Kapoor?
Answer: Do you expect her to don a traditional widow’s garb, and jump on a sacrificial pyre? Or would you prefer for her to become a celibate nun in some monastery? She’s moved on from her ex, and it seems like he has too. Would you say Arbaaz Khan also has loose morals, since he seems to be quite busy with Giorgia? You may not like Malaika Arora or Arjun Kapoor, but there is no need to call her a person of loose moral character. It just isn’t true. Who are we to pass judgment on others, when we don’t know the exact circumstances in their lives. Just let them be - both Malaika and Arbaaz have moved on, time for others to do so too.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Who is the wife of Ranveer Kapoor?
Answer: Since, you have essentially fused Ranveer Singh with Ranbir Kapoor, I suppose the wife must necessarily be a fusion of Deepika Padukone and Alia Bhatt. I surmise that the wife’s name must be either Deepika Bhatt or Alia Padukone. Pardon the persiflage - but you probably know the answer already to your question. If it’s Ranveer you were asking about, the answer is DP. If it’s Ranbir, then it’s Alia. There may well be a real life Ranveer Kapoor - if so, that person and his wife remain a mystery for me. Her name could be Julie, Nafisa, Priya, Harpreet, anything. One hardly knows what to speculate.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which movie will you watch Akshay Kumar's Raksha Bandhan or Aamir Khan Lal Singh Chadda since both are releasing on 11th of August?
Answer: Neither movie really appeals to me - one is going to be a boring remake of one of the most recognizable movies of all time. And, the trailer basically makes it look like PK has returned with a luxurious beard, to roam around planet earth again. Come on Aamir, couldn’t you make a movie with an original story? I’d love to see another Talaash or Sarfarosh from you, instead of seeing you constantly as a mentally challenged naive innocent character. The other is going to be a thinly disguised social issues movie masquerading as a comedy. Aanand L. Rai needs to get out of his comfort zone a bit now. All his movies are beginning to look like and feel the same. And Akki, please make a straight out masala action flick now - enough with the biopics and social issues flicks. Your hardcore original fanbase (I am one in that group) liked you because you were an action star - give us a couple of flicks like that. How impossible is it for you to toss us a Rowdy Rathore or a Sooryavanshi with more regularity? So, to sum it up - I’ll watch both movies grudgingly, and I am definitely not watching either in the theatre. Nope, I’ll wait for them to come on some streaming channel first.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Do you wear any protection when playing with a venomous snake?
Answer: When I play with venomous snakes, I ensure that I am always dressed appropriately for the sport in question. After all, “playing” with venomous snakes is a sure-shot guarantee of either, (a) being buried in a grave, (b) cremated in a crematorium, or, (c) placed on a tower, so a friendly flock of vultures can dine away on one’s inanimate corpse. It would not do to be dressed inappropriately in any of those cases - although, I suppose, one could get away by being disheveled for a crematorium. Honestly, if someone is “playing” with venomous snakes, they are pretty much displaying their utter imbecility. Venomous snakes are not pet puppies or kittens to play with - one bite, and you’re dead! So, instead of worrying about protection, ensure you’re dressed appropriately, because you really want to stand out in a dignified way, during your funeral, don’t you? Yes, you will be lying down mostly, but you still do want to stand out. Anyway, don’t PLAY with Venomous Snakes - they are not the ideal playmates, that you are imagining them to be.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which are some Bollywood actresses that slept with Boney Kapoor?
Answer: I am sure there are loads of scurrilous rumors hovering around Boney Kapoor. Many would make him out to be some sort of glamorous lothario. I have no idea if those rumors are true or not. They may or they may not be - one can hardly test the veracity of such rumors, unless one sticks like a leech to Boney’s pudgy tummy. But seeing that the late great star Sridevi, was his wife, I guess we can place Boney as having slept with at least one Bollywood actress namely Sridevi. But like I said, every other rumor may just simply be unsubstantiated scuttlebutt.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is a king cobra more dangerous than other cobras?
Answer: A King Cobra is terribly dangerous for cobras, while the proletariat or less-royal cobras are terribly dangerous for us hapless human beings. Of course, a King Cobra can easily kill a human with a single bite; however, King Cobras simply aren’t as dangerous for humans primarily because human-KC interactions are quite rare. King Cobras live very deep in the jungles, and very few naive humans usually hang around in those parts (those parts have a noticeable lack of ‘bars’, so it’s difficult to buy a beer or do a livestream to influence others there). It’s usually experts there who know how to handle the snakes and themselves. Also, consider this - you and I are in considerably more danger of being mugged or assaulted by some ordinary lout than we are of being assaulted or mugged by Prince Charles or some other Royal, right? Additionally, Kings are not as skittish as regular cobras are. The Spectacled cobra on the other hand is a proud member of the Big 4 of venomous snakes, which together kill more than 50,000 people annually in the greater Indian subcontinent. Kings barely kill a couple of people here and there, and a majority of times, those people are the ones who try to “kiss” the King Cobras. Consent is a rather important concept, isn’t it? Can’t say I blame the Kings here. To sum it all - King Cobras are not as dangerous as the regular common cobras. This is primarily due to the fact that regular cobras hang around people a lot more and are loads more skittish and bite people significantly more. But of course, the mighty mosquito is the most deadly and dangerous of all, and it isn’t even a snake.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How did "The Boys" series let so many people down?
Answer: It hasn’t let me down, but I do feel a tad bit disappointed that the show has rather veered off from the comicbook material. The show is kinda tame when compared to the comic, which was Uber subversive and to an ultimate extreme. Seriously, the show is pretty tame in comparison with the original Garth Ennis comics. Most of the other answers appear to be from folks who are perhaps not avid comicbook fans. I’m a bit of a purist, I’ve come to realize, in my expectations of how comics ought to be portrayed in film or television. I would like the original plots and stories depicted the way they appear in the comics. But I guess not as many folks really care about that. So anyway, the show is good; it’s just not as good as the original comics were. It’s not let me down - my own expectations seem to let me down.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why is Akshay Kumar a flop actor?
Answer: Akshay is not a flop actor - a few flops here and there do not make him a flop actor. After all, a person cannot have a 100% success rate in everything he or she does, can they? Prior to his current string of flops (Laxmii, Bell Bottom, Samrat Prithviraj, Bachchaan Paandey), he has given some big hits. We can’t forget the massive success of Sooryavanshi and Good Newwz, can we? So anyway, he’s not a flop actor - indeed, he’s been one of the most reliable stars in Bollywood for a while now. This current low phase isn’t even as bad as the one he had back in the 90s, where he had a continuous stream of 17 flops. I’m pretty sure he’ll bounce back. His stardom may be waning steadily, but that’s only inevitable thanks to the unceasing onslaught of Father Time.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Ranbir Kapoor's "Brahmastra" a flop movie?
Answer: We are peering into the (not-so-distant but nevertheless the) future here, since Bhramastra has not yet released. It releases in September, so there’s like two more months before we see whether or not it is a flop. Personally speaking, I am pretty confident that I will like the movie. It’s got actors I really like, such as Ranbir Kapoor, Amitabh Bachchan and Alia Bhatt. However, I am not as confident about my ability to predict its box office potential. There is a lot of finickiness in Indian movie audiences. They reject some really great movies, and then flock to some absolute mediocre fare. There is also the fact that Sci-Fi just hasn’t typically gotten great reactions among Indian audiences, so this was always a risky move. Finally, the many years of making have obviously bloated its budget - so, even if it does well, it may never recoup its cost. That could then result in a similar fate that befell Jagga Jasoos (which I personally adored!) So, while it’s not yet a flop movie, there are definitely prospects of it becoming a flop. I would of course prefer that it’s not, but I am not representative of the entire segment of movie going audiences. Let’s hope it does exceedingly well, but if it doesn’t, then I’m afraid the movie may well end up as a flop.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why does Mr. Reeves look so miserable standing next to Alex Grant?
Answer: He does not look miserable standing next to Alexandra Grant. I believe it is projection on your part - perhaps, you would like to see Keanu with a much more nubile partner, like so many other Hollywood stars are wont to do? Or perhaps you’ve seen only pictures of Keanu in his resting face - I mean the man can’t plaster a smile on his face every single moment in perpetuity. Anyway, here’s a collage of him looking distinctly happy while with Alexandra. So, if you search through their pics together, you’ll find a bunch more just like the ones I’ve put in this answer. He does not look miserable next to her - if he was, do you think he’d be thinking of marrying her?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why has Vidya Balan never worked with Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, and Aamir Khan?
Answer: She’s just never been offered a role opposite any of the trio. For better or for worse, Vidya Balan has slotted herself into a “serious actress” category. Our Khan trio rarely if ever make uber-serious movies. So, at the outset, there just isn’t a natural fit. Likewise, Vidya Balan is now 43 years old, which makes her significantly younger than our Khan triumvirate, who are all in their upper-50s. But in most movie industries’ logic, an actress who is 40+ is almost always “aged out”. Our Khan trio (especially Aamir and Salman) come with really younger actresses, so Vidya is out of luck there. So, unless the Khan trio make an uber-realistic movie, there really is no chance of seeing Vidya Balan appearing opposite them. Out of the trio though, I think the best prospects are to see her with Shahrukh, but those are pretty low too. So, I suppose, we just have to be satisfied to see her with Shahrukh during the latter’s cameo in Heyy Baby.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is a non-venomous snake all safe?
Answer: Not if you’re just the right size for a starving Reticulated Python. Then despite the lack of venom, a loving squeeze will ensue, and after that, it’ll all be rather pitch black with some gastric juices sploshing about. But honestly, non-venomous and even venomous snakes have more to fear from humans, rather than the other way around. We kill indiscriminately, and out of fearful and moronic ignorance. And other non-venomous snakes can still bite you - it won’t be a venomous bite, but will still pain. So, do exercise caution, and leave them alone!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is there really going to be a GI Jane 2 starring Jada Pinkett Smith?
Answer: Well, if there is a GI Jane 2 movie made, that is only going to land the beleaguered Will Smith, and his stardom in further hot soup. That is even more likely if this movie ends up casting Jada in it. His role in the infamous slapgate will seem even more useless and moronic, if we end up with a GI Jane 2, starring Jada. Basically, it’ll ruin his stardom even worse. But I doubt they’re going to make a GI Jane 2. The first one wasn’t really successful; so, it’s highly doubtful that the studio will bankroll a sequel. Maybe in another decade or so, they could make a loosely connected reboot or sequel, but as of now, the prospects of a sequel are infinitesimal, and the prospects drop even further when one considers Jada to be starring in it.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why isn't Raj Babbar more famous than Amitabh Bachchan, even though he is a better actor than the latter?
Answer: Well, even if we consider the claim that Raj Babbar is a better actor than Amitabh Bachchan, the fact is that acting prowess does not correlate with fame. Lady Luck is a very fickle mistress, and does not care a hoot for one’s acting ability. She smiled a lot more at Amitabh Bachchan, and a lot less at Raj Babbar; hence, the disparity in their respective fame levels. But I don’t agree that Raj Babbar is a better actor than Amitabh - the latter is a tremendous actor, and more importantly (from the p.o.v. of fame) a bigger superstar. One can admire them both, but their acting styles are quite different to be directly compared. Like I said earlier, luck is a better predictor of why one became more famous than the other. Acting ability has nothing to do with it. For all you know, the greatest actor in the universe may be languishing in some village play, just because Lady Luck is frowning at him or her. P.S. - It is no secret that the two actors don’t get along at all. I always thought it was due to their differing political philosophies, but it turns out Rekha was also a bone of contention between them. Rather interesting…

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why would a luxury car company like Bugatti dare to blacklist the famous actor Tom Cruise?
Answer: Oh, I looked this up. Apparently, they weren’t happy that Tom Cruise wasn’t able to open one of the doors. During some event for MI:3, Tom came to the premiere with his then wife Katie Holmes, in a Bugatti Veyron. After getting down, he went over to Katie’s side to open the door for her, but struggled to get it open. It took a little bit of time for the door to be opened. Something different about the car, I guess, that makes it hard to open from the outside. The ever available paparazzi and others of their ilk took a bunch of pics and videos of that incident. The Bugatti powers-that-be were definitely not happy with their car looking like some sort of malfunctioning junker. So, they then put Tom Cruise on a blacklist. That blacklist btw is pretty meaningless- if Tom Cruise wants a Bugatti, there are other ways by which he can procure one. He can get someone else to buy it on his behalf, or he could buy a gently used one. Heck, if you’re reading this Tom, give me the moolah to buy one, and I’ll buy one for you, and I’ll personally drive it up and deliver it to you ;) What could be a better deal than that? I also promise you won’t have to open my door from the outside either.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What character do you think would scare the Joker in a confrontation?
Answer: I think they depicted this in an actual comic - The Punisher quite scared the Joker, and then, Batsie had to come save the Clown Prince from The Punisher. I’m just not sure whether this comic is canon or not. I think this would be pretty accurate though. With Batman, Joker knows that Batsie will never kill him. He will be off for a little holiday in Arkham Asylum, and then back to causing chaos soon after. NO Chance of that ever happening with only Frank Castle involved. One bullet (or many), and it’s bye-bye Joker. And, he knows it! Another person that could possibly scare the Joker is Billy Butcher from Boys - but I’m not so sure really. Billy Butcher would probably recruit the Joker into his squad. So, I guess, Frank Castle as the Punisher, remains my pick for this question.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which characters are way better in comic books than in the movies?
Answer: There are two comicbook characters, both of whom are among the pantheon of my favorite villains. I refer to Gorr the God Butcher from Thor, and Doomsday from Superman. We first saw a version of Doomsday in Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice. Let me just say that it was the heights of injustice to call that travesty of a clay model as Doomsday. It didn’t look like Doomsday, but rather like some sort of misshaped troll made of clay. The second one, which I am mighty disappointed with is the MCU’s portrayal of Gorr the God Butcher. The MCU has BUTCHERED the look - this Christian Bale version looks NOTHING like Gorr. Looks more like that albino priest from that Da Vinci Code movie than he does Gorr. I’m still praying that the MCU is just pulling their usual fake trailer stunt, and that the real authentic Gorr will be presented in the movies. But I’m not holding my breath for that particular miracle to occur.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What was the Lars Von Trier movie that managed to excite a lot of people?
Answer: Well, the answer to this question is possibly the duology of the two Nymphomaniac movies. Actually, scratch that - I think the Lars von Trier movie that managed to excite a lot of people is the first movie in the duology. I refer to Nymphomaniac: Vol 1. After people saw the movie, and realized that all of the sex in the movie was far, far, and did I say far, away from being sexy, I bet the excitement died out for the next movie. The titillation quotient of both these movies is absurdly low. The movies are both rather disturbing, as most Lars von Trier movies tend to be. So, I would say that people got excited about the Nymphomaniac duology, due to all the rampant sex promised in it. Many were probably expecting some sort of auteurish homage to Ron Jeremy or John Holmes’ movies - what they got instead was a disturbing tragedy, with lots of extremely clinical looking sex. That sort of stuff rarely excites anyone - if someone got excited by either of the Nymphomaniac movies, then well, they are obviously individuals with exceedingly great libidinous fortitude. P.S. - The image above shows Shia LaBeouf displaying the countenance of an audience member who was excepting something entirely different from the Nymphomaniac duology.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is the super famous celebrity and Bollywood actress Disha Patani a Gujarati Indian?
Answer: No, Disha Patani is not a Gujarati. I’m not sure why anyone would think she is - I suppose, someone not familiar with Indian names, could obliquely compare her name with Amisha Patel, and think Disha Patani is similar (i.e. because of the ‘Isha’ and ‘Pat’ similarity in their names). But the two names really are quite different, and the two actresses hail from completely different linguistic and state backgrounds. Disha Patani is basically a Kumaoni with Rajput roots, and is from Uttarkhand. So, quite far from Gujarat. Therefore, she is not a Gujarati, but is an Uttakhandi, and to be more specific, a Kumaoni.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Are saltwater crocodiles immune to black mamba snake venom?
Answer: Sadly, one may never know how immune Salties are to Mamba venom. Unless, of course, a great ‘reunification’ happens, and all the continents recombobulate and join up to reveal a brand new Pangaea. Then, we can see how immune a Saltie is to Black Mamba venom. But right now, it’s practically impossible for a Saltie to careen over to a Mamba, let alone be bitten by one, for us to be able to verify the immunity. Similarly, Mamba’s aren’t exactly going to get a Red Carpet welcome in Australia - sad, but true. I mean, Australia already has its own homegrown crop of venomous snakes - why would they need to go start importing snakes from other continents? If the immunity being discussed had to do with the incredible yearning people feel when faced with indelible beauty, then well, nobody is immune to Black Mambas. Salties will obviously fall head-over-heels in love with the nubile and rather pulchritudinous Mambas, biological constraints be damned. But I gather, you’re inquiring about immunity from actual venom, so of course, there is no point in talking about unrequited love here. But if there ever was a beauty contest in snakes, Black Mambas would be on the top of the list. Anyway, persiflage aside, I highly doubt that Black Mamba venom is dangerous to Salties, unless the Saltie has an open wound, and the Mamba methodically bites through that open wound. And even then, you’d probably need like a dozen or so Mambas all operating in unison, for it to do any damage to the Saltie.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the danger of handling a black mamba?
Answer: The biggest danger is of course that the Mamba bites the bejesus out of you. Two drops of Mamba venom are quite enough to kill an adult human being. Some of the usual symptoms involve “pleasant symptoms” like paralysis, hyper-salivation, dizziness, and hemorrhage. Oh, and it’s going to pain worse than a dentist yanking your teeth out with a blunt rusty spanner. Then, if you don’t get rushed to the hospital, and heaven forbid, they don’t have any antivenom, then by golly, you are definitely dead. Handling the Black Mamba casually is a recipe for disaster, and one may as well arrange for one’s last will to be arranged beforehand. Handling a Black Mamba (by a nonexpert) is basically seeking out an appointment with death.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is your honest review on Prabhas starrer movie Radhe Shyam?
Answer: This was one of the most insipid and boring Telugu movies I’ve ever seen. Prabhas looked awfully bored in the movie, from start to finish. It Feels like he realized after the first day of shooting that the film was going to be a massive Turkey, and then simply went through the motions. I did too - I watched it rather disinterestedly, and realized that nothing really stood out in the movie, nor was remotely memorable. Not the acting, not the story, not the direction, and definitely not the music. Yes, it’s been shot really well, and Pooja Hegde does her best to look as beautiful as she can. But her doing so doesn’t change the fact that Prabhas continues to appear listless and dull throughout the movie. Prior to shooting the film, the director should have consulted an astrologer to ascertain whether or not the movie would work with such a poor plot - a good astrologer may have well saved the day. But no such luck, alas! That’s my honest review of the movie - what, I didn’t reveal much of the movie in this review? Well yes, I didn’t remember too much of it in the end - it’s basically an anachronistic love story with a poorly developed plot about a palmist and his doomed fortune, as it relates to his romantic life. Watch it for yourself to see how boring and dull it is! At best, you’ll discover its soporific qualities.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How can Amber Heard salvage her career after losing her defamation trial with Johnny Depp?
Answer: I really don’t see any sort of quick salvaging of her career in movies or entertainment or modeling. As an actress or glamorous performer, she is pretty much done, at least in the short term horizon. But memory is a fickle creature, and if Amber Heard lays low (not too low) for a few years, while doing acts of good and appearing contrite etc., she may yet get a reprieve in the future. Perhaps, some indie director or producer will wish to give her a chance. But as a main lead in mainstream Hollywood movies, her career is pretty over (and not ‘over’ in the WWE sense). She may have a future as a supporting actress of some sort though. Like, I could see her come in a AHS season or two - not right now, but perhaps in the future. She could easily come as a daughter of Kathy Bates’ character. But I’m not ruling her out completely in the world of entertainment, even in the short term horizon. Someone in an answer (can’t recall who, but I had upvoted that answer a few days/weeks back) had suggested that Amber Heard could perhaps work in the WWE. I can actually see that happening - she could act like the consummate heel in an edgy story, but that may not work out long term. It’ll probably be a short storyline. So yeah, I’m not saying that her career is completely impossible to salvage, but it’ll take a lot of effort on her part to improve her reputation.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Talia al Ghul a good guy or a bad guy?
Answer: Well, for starters, unless they are planning a massive and bound to be unpopular retcon of sorts, Talia is not really a guy at all. She’s always been depicted as a beautiful and dangerously capable woman in all the Batman comics. As far as being a villain is concerned, sometimes she’s a villain and sometimes she’s not. She’s not a villain like the Joker for instance - sometimes, she’s even helped Batman and friends. But all things considered, she is a bit of both. Sometimes good, and sometimes bad - but from a purely moral standpoint, she is rather steeped in crime.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Alexandra Daddario a bad actress, or is she misunderstood?
Answer: She is definitely not a bad actress - I have liked her in the many roles she’s done. I also don’t think she is in any way misunderstood. I mean, what’s there to misunderstand? The “know-it-all” types who criticize her for her acting skills usually do that for all actors/actresses out there. It’s almost like they believe in their omnipotence in all things acting related. Perceptions do vary on judging the acting prowess of others, don’t you know? From all I’ve seen of her, she’s been decent enough in the movie and tv shows I’ve seen her in. I mean consider a movie like Baywatch - sure the movie wasn’t great, but were people expecting her to act differently in it? She was playing a lifeguard in it after all. She was great in her small role in True Detective as well. Yes, she has some good movies and some terrible ones - but the same is true of other actresses out there. Anyway, for me at least, she is not a terrible actress.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What do you think about Gorr's look in Thor: Love and Thunder?
Answer: It’s bloody awful! The MCU has butchered the look of Gorr the God Butcher! Who the F cares that it’s Christian Bale playing Gorr, if he doesn’t look like Gorr? He bloody well looks like the albino priest from that Da Vinci movie. What’s next? For a live action Mickey Mouse movie, are they going to insist that the actor playing the titular role have his own face on there? More man less mouse? I was so looking forward to this movie, and now it feels more like a Thor’vinci Code movie than the epic flick I was praying for! Ah hell, maybe Gorr was right!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why aren't people employing Daisy Ridley?
Answer: Well, I can only speak for myself, but there is no way I could employ Daisy Ridley. I mean, her net worth is in millions of dollars (9 million prior to this horrid market crash). So, suffice to say, I could never employ Daisy Ridley for anything. It’s easier for me to ask the Daisy next door to act in a play for me or some such. I would imagine that’s the case for most people ;) But as far as real producers are concerned - they are indeed employing and hiring Daisy Ridley for a variety of roles. While she may not be getting the roles you think she ought to, she isn’t in any trouble of having her career disappear from beneath her. There is the fact though that she seems to be devoting equal time to her voiceover jobs - so, that perhaps ends up giving the impression that she’s not actively in movies. She is though, and her busy list of projects is testament to that. She really isn’t in any danger of disappearing - even if she retires from on-screen work (and, I doubt that!), she will remain a sought out voiceover artist.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: How do you think Giancarlo Esposito would fare in the role of Batman?
Answer: He would be utterly miscast as Batsie. I could easily see him essay the role of Lucius Fox though - he’d be perfect as that! But as Batsie, he’d be a no-go, from my point of view. He doesn’t work as an older Batsie either. Besides Lucius Fox, I can see him in other roles in the Batman world - for instance, he could play Commissioner Gordon or he could play an older version of Scarecrow. But really, Lucius Fox is the role he can play with subtle elan. That would be a perfect casting, I think!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Jessica Alba sick?
Answer: The other answer insinuating that she has herpes is relying on some sort of scurrilous rumors. A disgruntled ex-employee basically spread the herpes rumors, but those are unsubstantiated rumors. Additionally, Jessica Alba is not currently sick with any illness - she mentioned during an interview last year, that she had a lot of heath related issues during her childhood. She apparently had chronic allergies, and suffered from partially collapsed lungs, pneumonia and tonsillar cysts. And, these health issues resurfaced during her first pregnancy. So, my guess is that her chronic allergies resurfaced during her first pregnancy, and probably caused her a lot of stress. She also suffered from anxiety disorder in her early 20s, and wishes that she had sought out therapy for it then. So basically, I am not aware of any sickness that she is suffering from at present - the interview in which she mentioned her heath related issues only talked about her past issues. She is pretty healthy as of now, and hopefully continues to remain so.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why don't Indians typically eat fast food?
Answer: They actually do, and plenty of it too - almost every fast food type of place exists in India. Of course, those brands do need to de-beefify and de-porkify their menus, and make sure to have lots of vegetarian options. Usually, Mutton ends up being the replacement for beef and pork. I’m sure you can find some which have beef and pork items, but generally, it’s bound to be chicken-item heavy. Additionally, Indians have other “fast food” options, such as the Idlis, Upmas, Dosas etc., which are relatively fast to obtain as well. I gather though that you were inquiring about American based fast food. So, Indians definitely do eat fast food - they probably wouldn’t if they didn’t have anything to eat there (e.g. if the menu had nothing for them). But the offerings in India ensure there are items for the locals to be able to eat.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Are you disappointed with how Gorr (played by Christian Bale) looks in the new Thor movie?
Answer: I quite certainly am disappointed - the movie version of Gorr looks nothing like the comic version. This Bale version looks a bit like that albino priest from the Da Vinci Code. Not in the slightest like our favorite Butcher of Gods. The reason they’re giving for deviating from Gorr’s look is that they want to showcase Christian Bale’s real life look. Dumb logic, that! They could have made him look more comic appropriate rather than what they’ve made him look now. I really was looking forward to this movie, but this shoddy version of Gorr is ticking me off.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why did Hollywood actor Leonardo DiCaprio praise the Bollywood actress Urvashi Rautela at the Cannes Film Festival 2022?
Answer: According to Urvashi, Leo complimented her and praised her for being a talented actress. I suppose Leo praised her because he saw her in wonderful movies like Hate Story 4 and Virgin Bhanupriya. Hmm… possible, perhaps? Actually scratch that - I don’t think Leo would have praised her for being a talented actress. At most, he may have praised her for looking beautiful in her black gown or something. If he did praise her for being a talented actress, then it must just be lip service. I really doubt he’s seen any of her movies. There are great odds of Urvashi simply having made up the whole tale, but if indeed, Leo did praise her, it was not for her being a talented actress. At most, I can believe that he praised her for looking beautiful in her black gown.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the full truth of Urfi Javed? How much does she earn to expose her body?
Answer: I have seen Urfi Javed mostly on Instagram, where it appears like a bunch of paparazzi keep following her, and taking pics and videos of her. I thought she was another Instagram influencer of sorts. Turns out she’s a television actress, and I suspect she wants to get into Bollywood movies, eventually. I am not a fan of how this question is worded though. Urfi is obviously trying her best to be noticed by directors or producers. Why try to shame her by phrasing your query the way you have? I have no idea what her professional compensation charges are, but I’d have to say that she probably expects a fair amount of compensation for any acting or modeling gigs. She is definitely not afraid of posing in glamorous clothes, so there you have it.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Was Russell Crowe ashamed of his body weight?
Answer: That’s what some articles are speculating. Apparently, he’s decided to avoid the public gaze for a while. He is seemingly embarrassed about his burgeoning weight, especially because some of the pictures are hardly flattering. Anyway, he’ll probably be able to lose the weight soon enough - Hollywood celebs usually never have too much trouble doing so. They have the best trainers available, and what’s more - he acquired the weight for a role he’s doing. When his next role comes around, he’ll easily get back to shape. While he won’t likely start looking like he’s 30 again, he will definitely have no trouble looking fitter for sure.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why can’t the Hindi movie industry Bollywood afford to make films with Telugu film superstar actor Mahesh Babu?
Answer: I’m sure they can afford him, but what they can’t afford is to get him the kind of adulation he frequently gets in Tollywood. His comment about “They can’t afford me” was made in light of that. The kind of respect and power he commands in Tollywood; he will almost certainly never get in Bollywood. I mean consider when he did the Tamil version of Spyder, he was criticized pretty severely by Tamil critics. That would not have been appreciated by him, for sure. In contrast, Telugu critics are much kinder to him, and of course, his fans totally worship him. That level of fan worship will not be forthcoming from a wholly Bollywood fan base. If he appears in Hindi movies, expect something similar. Toxic troll reviewers like KRK will have a field time blasting Mahesh Babu for everything - who would want to endure all that? It’s kinda like, he’s happy being a top dog in his Tollywood, rather than being a mid-carder in Bollywood.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Do you think “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness” should have been rated R?
Answer: Not at all - a PG 13 rating was just fine for Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. As per me (and as per the MPAA, apparently), a movie replete with profanity deserves an R rating more than a movie with violence. The only bits of rude language I can remember hearing in this movie are ‘crap’ and ‘ass’, which aren’t really profanity any longer. Only F-words and their cousinly iterations are considered profanity nowadays, I think. Yes, there were humans and inhumans (and demons and monsters etc.) getting killed on screen, but the movie didn’t show them getting gruesomely killed like they would in a Texas Chainsaw Massacre type of movie. If the movie had Dr. Strange or Wanda or Wong or America hurling a bunch of F-bombs in it, then the movie would have deserved a R. Or if they showed gruesome scenes of gore, then an R-rating would be well deserved. But in its current form, I did not think the movie should have been rated R. I mean, come on, it’s Sam Raimi directing the movie - he is an expert in skirting the line between PG-13 and R ratings, and I think he did so quite masterfully in this film as well.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Should Lex Luger be in the WWF Hall of Fame already?
Answer: Yes, he totally should! Lex Luger may not have been the greatest in-ring workers, but then he didn’t need to! He needed to look like He-Man, and basically show off his impressive physique in the ring. In fact, during his earlier days, he was expressly told to focus on showcasing his body. That’s what he did. His signature move, ‘The Torture Rack’ was designed to show off his muscles and physique. And, he totally was - he looked amazing, and his heel persona was fantastic. His babyface persona wasn’t as good, but boy, he looked great in that too. Apart from that, the death of Miss Elizabeth should not be blamed on Lex Luger. He didn’t pump the drugs into her, and cause the overdose. He and she were both taking drugs and alcohol, and she sadly overdid it. Lex is the one who called the paramedics in the first place. And, he did not beat or hit Miss Elizabeth prior to that. The charges were filed due to an overzealous police officer, who did not even listen to Miss Elizabeth, when she loudly insisted that Lex never hurt her. Her injuries were caused as a result of her loosing her balance and hitting the hard pavement, due to their two big dogs’ (a GSD and a Husky or Akita) leashes getting entangled with her feet. The charges were eventually dropped - so it’s a bit absurd to call him an abuser. Anyway, comparing Lex with the heinous Benoit is absurd - they are not in the slightest bit similar. I hope they put Lex into the HoF soon - get him in there, and get Sting to induct him into it. Lex has totally changed in his outlook to life, after he got religious. He seems very contrite about his past misdeeds, but those misdeeds are not HoF ban worthy misdeeds. Bring the Total Package into the HoF! High time! P.S. - I got all this info about Lex, from his fascinating autobiography (Wrestling with the Devil). Give it a read - very compelling stuff.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What unrealistic thing in Harry Potter is never talked about?
Answer: Umm… Harry Potter has giants, ogres, dragons, witches, wizards, house-elves, werewolves, ghosts, and pixies in it. And yet, we have people bemoaning the fact that “it’s unrealistic”. “This sort of thing could never happen in real life”, these critics wail and gnash their teeth! For crying out loud - it’s not meant to be realistic! Yes, there are elements from it that you can take and metaphorically apply to reality. Cornelius Fudge for instance is a typical politician - any country, any context, you’ll have a dozen Fudges, at the very least. Same thing with Dolores Umbridge - you want to meet an Umbridge in real life? Go up to your local HOA, and demand to to speak with its president. Whoever it is is damn-near-guaranteed to be just like Umbridge. So, I find this criticism about Harry Potter being unrealistic to be absolute bonkers! What’ll be next - more wailing about the fact that the Harry Potter series never has a reality arc that talks about how students are getting pregnant there, and Dumbledore is shipping all of the unwanted babies off to a dwarf mine in the LOTR world? For gosh’s sake - it’s a fantastical world, and not meant to be “realistic!” If you’re reading Harry Potter, and expecting it to be a dreary old realistic book, then perhaps, it just isn’t the book series for you! I would recommend something else for you, but the sordid truth is that I never read realistic fiction. I crave the fantastic, the impossible - that’s what I like. I want to escape into a world we never see in reality - if I want to experience reality, I’ll just jolly well do so in real life. Why read a book for that?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What are Sam Raimi's best movies?
Answer: Sam Raimi is one of my favorite directors. He’s made many great classic movies - he’s often thought of as a horror movie director, but he’s pretty versatile. In fact, he doesn’t do as much horror nowadays. I wish he would make a few more bone-chilling horror flicks; but oh well, I am looking forward to the new Doctor Strange sequel. Anyway, some of his best movies include the original Evil Dead series, the first Spider-Man movie, The Quick and the Dead, Drag Me to Hell, and The Gift. The last one has Keanu Reeves in a antagonist role, and it’s quite a great flick. You really can’t go wrong with any Sam Raimi movie - even if they’re not great, they’re never terrible.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: You are a mother crocodile. You see a honey badger raiding your nest. You try to scare it off, but the honey badger wants to stand and fight. How can you kill the honey badger and save what's left of your nest?
Answer: I appreciate the efforts to mythicize honey badgers, but this is a serious mismatch in reality. It’s possibly a bigger mismatch than me wrestling a no holds barred Hell-in-a-Cell match with Brock Lesnar. Unless the world has gone topsy turvy, Adult Crocodiles greatly outweigh and dwarf any Honey Badgers out there. All the momma croc has to do is grab the raiding honey badger, and crunch him/her up as a light afternoon snack. There is no chance in hell of the honey badger surviving a stand-off with an adult Nile crocodile. Momma croc wins, each and every time!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What are the factors for the failure of the 2022 Telugu movie Archarya? Is it right to compare Archarya with Akhanda since both movies share the same themes?
Answer: Well, the biggest factor for the failure of the film is the sloppy and dull script. Truly, what an abysmally dull script it is - for a movie about ‘mining’, all it succeeds in doing is ‘boring’ its audience. An utter waste to have this movie be the one that has Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan together. They deserved a better script, and a better director. The cinematography looks crisp though, and the father-son chemistry together is undeniable. They should look for a better script next time, as with a better script, I think their combo will be extremely successful. Pooja Hegde is alright, but really has very minuscule scope. Anyway, I didn’t think the movie was similar to Akhanda at all - quite different really. For all its faults and predictability, Akhanda was not boring like Acharya. Any case, Boyapati movies are never known for their riveting scripts, but Koratala Siva used to be. I guess, unrealistic audience expectations also played a part here in amping up the boring factor. It’s like if you are expecting something remarkable, and get a plate of an old dull hash, your negative reactions are much more visceral.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Has Amber Heard lost most of her fans?
Answer: She has definitely lost any fans who became fans of hers because she was married to Johnny Depp. You know the Depp fans who became her fans simply because she was married to him. However, she must have retained at least a small portion of the fans that she had prior to her being married to Johnny Depp. After all, she was a beautiful model and actress, in her own right, and has appeared as a lead actress in movies. And, there are still plenty of people around who support her over Johnny Depp (you can see plenty of them right here on Quora) - I would assume that those folks are still her fans. But overall yes, she seems to have lost the PR battle, and so has definitely lost a lot of fans, even if it’s not most of her fans.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Did Thor: Love and Thunder make the right move in casting Natalie Portman as Lady Thor? What is your unedited opinion about it?
Answer: Natalie Portman played Jane Foster in the first two Thor movies - so, I guess, it’s good that she’s back in this movie, just for continuity’s sake. And, while she didn’t seem in the slightest bit interested in the role in the first two Thor movies, she does seem more interested this time around. I suppose, she’s a fan of Taika Waititi, and also Chris Hemsworth is a much bigger star this time around. So, hopefully, she’ll look better in this film. As far as “Lady Thor” is concerned, the comics never actually refer to her as Lady Thor. She simply becomes the Goddess of Thunder, and Thor gives her the right to use his name (and renounces the name himself). So, she’s called Thor by everyone in the comics (except for a cranky Odin and belligerent Cul, if I recall correctly). She is addressed as “My Lady” on occasion by the genial gourmand Volstagg. But nobody calls her “Lady Thor” - for all practical purposes, she is simply called Thor. I don’t know if the movie is going to change all of that drastically, but it looks like they will have to make many changes, because honestly, Jane only becomes Thor much after Gorr is already dispatched with, in the comics. In the movie, I guess they’ll show both Thors fighting together in unison against Gorr. Anyway, my unedited opinion is that it is fine to have Natalie Portman as Thor in the new movie. She was Jane Foster in the first two flicks, and as long as the movie isn’t rebooted, she should be Jane Foster in the remaining Thor movies.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Since Charli XCX is Indian, is she the most popular and successful Bollywood star?
Answer: I have no idea how you knew that I’m a fan of Charli XCX, but hell yeah, I’ve been totally binging on her music this past month! :) I totally love her songs and her super stylish videos! But, here’s the thing - she is not Indian, at least not citizenship wise, and she’s definitely not a Bollywood star. She is Indian-Origin, but you can’t call her Indian, because the best classification of her ethnic roots would be Indo-Scott, since her dad is Scottish, while her mom is Indian (albeit from Uganda). She is British (her Wikipedia page lists her as English), but I thought the correct way to classify is British not English. Anyway, all that is immaterial - what is germane is that Charli XCX is AWESOME! I certainly do hope that I can see her in a concert one day!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Growing up I loved Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, and Chow Yun Fat films. Given the choice, which of the three actors’ films do you appreciate the most?
Answer: Oh, Jackie for me all the way! I LOVE Jackie Chan - one of my all time favorite actors. I grew up watching Jackie Chan and Sammo Hung movies - for me, they’re almost like distant uncles in a way, y’know! I will always be a fan of Jackie Chan. I like Bruce Lee and Chow Yun Fat too, but Jackie’s my all-time-favorite! His movies stand the test of time for me - I still enjoy watching his Police Story movies. Those are just the best action flicks, and Jackie’s comedy mixup in many of his films is brilliant. Additionally, he’s a fab actor, and can do a variety of roles, equally well. He obviously excels in action-comedy, but he can do romance and drama well too. Anyone, who says otherwise has obviously not seen Shinjuku Incident or Gorgeous.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Between Hollywood’s Amber Heard and Johnny Depp, who would you advise to meet the famous Indian spiritualist Sadhguru for their mental well-being?
Answer: Honestly, between Johnny Depp and Amber Heard, I am rather firmly ensconced in Johnny’s corner. I think it is quite appalling how Amber Heard has destroyed Johnny Depp’s career and life. I hope he can get his career back on track somewhat, after all this courtroom drama. While I don’t wish Amber Heard any harm, you will not find me praying for her career revival, quite as fervently either. As far as advising either of them to meet Sadhguru for their mental well-being is concerned, I am firmly of the opinion that anyone wishing to improve their mental well-being should do so, however they want. So, if either Johnny or Amber believe that meeting Sadhguru will improve their well-being, then they should definitely go ahead and meet him. It is really important to have equanimity of mind, and I am pretty sure both Johnny and Amber need that tranquility in their lives (the former more so, of course!) Anyway, I really do hope Johnny Depp can get his career back on track - he’s a wonderful actor, and it would be a pity to never see him on screen again. A real pity, and a crying shame!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is Will Smith doing in Mumbai?
Answer: At first, I thought that he’s gone to Mumbai to lie low for a bit. After all, his stock has plummeted here in the US, so why not go to a place, where he’s always gotten a lot of adulation and love. He is quite adored in India. But then another report surfaced, and it turns out that Will Smith went to India to meet with a spiritual leader, Sadhguru. I suppose Will realizes that he needs to work on his inner wellbeing - so, I suppose this trip is in order to work on that. It also has the optics to help him makeover his now dented public persona, a bit. Hopefully, it’ll work and he can re-emerge as an emotionally secure and happier person. Edit - oh Sadhguru’s team has clarified that Sadhguru isn’t even in India right now. So, I guess my initial line of thought was correct - Will has gone to India for a bit of relaxation and effort to find some tranquility of mind, even if he’s not meeting Sadhguru.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Megan Fox the most beautiful woman in the world?
Answer: Maybe she isn’t for some, maybe she is for some. But she is definitely the most beautiful woman in the world for her present fiancé, Machine Gun Kelly. Based on their various interactions and Instagram posts, it looks like he’s the most handsome man in the world, as per her, as well. And, I’m sure that there are plenty of diehard Megan Fox fans who will also consider her to be the most beautiful woman in the world. But really, this is a question seeking an objective answer to a rather subjective question - the answer is, it depends on who’s evaluating the question. If MGK is, then we know that she is definitely the Queen of his heart.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Who is your favorite Bond girl?
Answer: There are about twenty-one answers to this question, and nary a one has even mentioned my personal favorite Bond Girl. I refer to the beautiful Izabella Scorupco who played Natalya Simonova in Goldeneye. This movie is my most favorite Bond movie, and so, I suppose it makes sense that my favorite Bond Girl is from this very movie. I’m a little disappointed that she didn’t get a whole lot of movies after Goldeneye. I’d have really loved to have seen her in more big budget films. Yes, she came in several others, but nothing quite as big as the Bond film. She was perfect in Goldeneye.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Does Thor love Peter Quill (aka Star-Lord), in a romantic way, and not in a brotherly love or platonic kind of way? What evidence do you have?
Answer: No, Thor does not love Peter Quill in a romantic way. Thor is and has always been depicted as having heterosexual leanings and desires. I mean, read any of his comics or even the actual Norse legends, Thor is straight, and really has no issues being romantically cosy with women of any species, be they Asgardians, Giants, Dwarves, Humans, or any other species. You're probably asking this because of that little joke in the new Thor movie teaser. That’s just a Taika Waititi joke to show how eager Thor is. Nothing in it to suggest any unrequited romantic links between Thor and Peter Quill.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which actress gets a movie role because she is close with the movie director?
Answer: Sheri Moon Zombie, the wife of Rob Zombie, comes to mind. All of her movie roles, with the exception of Toolbox Murders have been directed by Rob Zombie. Yes, all of her movie roles, including Halloween, The Devil’s Rejects, The Lords of Salem etc etc, were directed by her Hubby dearest. Well, she’s also appeared in two television show episodes, one on Californication and one on CSI: Miami. One of those episodes was (wait for it!) also directed by Rob Zombie. So, I guess she fits this question really well. Any movie Rob Zombie makes, Sheri Moon Zombie will have a role in. I don’t see anything wrong with it, by the way. I mean if you won’t help your family members out in their careers and passions, then what good are you, right? Rob’s alright!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Are Arjun Kapoor and Shraddha Kapoor siblings?
Answer: Well, no, they are not siblings. Far from it, and they’re not cousins either - they are from entirely different Kapoor families altogether. Arjun is from the Boney Kapoor family, while Shraddha is from the Shakti Kapoor family. Also, consider how icky it would be for siblings to work as the lead pair in a romantic movie like Half Girlfriend? The movie was a strictly watch-one-time flick; if the lead pair were siblings, then yuck, the movie would have been completely unwatchable. Well okay, it may have been a big hit in parts of the world where such close “romantic links” are heartily appreciated. But thankfully, that was not the case here. So to repeat again, Arjun and Shraddha Kapoor are not siblings. And in case, one thinks of this other link - Aditya Roy Kapoor is also completely unrelated to Shraddha and Arjun.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the saddest thing about the Bollywood actress Anushka Sharma?
Answer: From the outside looking in, one can’t really detect a whole lot of things to feel sad for Anushka. From all possible factors, things seem to be going well. She’s happily married, a happy parent, successful in business, and getting set to stage a movie comeback, etc etc. However, the reality is we don’t really know. There may be a bunch of things she’s having the need to be sad about in her life - we just don’t know about them, and won’t know, unless she choses to share them with outsiders. But we do certainly hope that if there are reasons for her to be sad, then those sadness causing reasons can be ameliorated.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the most epic "one take" song ever recorded?
Answer: For me, it’s gotta be Gwen Stefani’s “Make Me Like You” music video, which was recorded live in front of the Grammy Awards audience back in 2016. An epic song, and a lovely video too. I really can’t believe it was shot in one take! Mighty brave, and gutsy move, that! Gwen Stefani totally rocks! Check out that song and video!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which Hollywood actor or actress who is currently embattled in the legal system do you feel a sense of utmost melancholy for?
Answer: I totally love Michael Madsen. I’ve loved him since I first saw him in Species and Reservoir Dogs. His drawling style of talking is just sublime, and I just enjoy watching him in whatever he’s in. So, I recently read about his getting arrested; I was rather taken aback by that news. He was apparently arrested for trespassing at a house from where he’d been evicted. He looked disheveled and somewhat out-of-it during the arrest. But the eviction and arrest isn’t why I felt a sense of melancholy - it was the underlying reason behind Michael Madsen’s mental breakdown. His son (US Army Sgt. Hudson Madsen) committed suicide back in January. That must have led Michael Madsen to have a complete breakdown, which led to this eventual arrest. They are most definitely linked. The poor guy - I can’t imagine how shocked and sad he must be. I feel really sorry for him, and hope he can get the help he needs. P.S - If you’re feeling suicidal please seek out help - there are resources out there. Don’t go through with it. You may think you’re choosing the easy way out, but you’re leaving behind a minefield dotted with mines for those who love you.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Can I hang out with Bollywood actresses if I produce a Bollywood movie?
Answer: Sure, why you could even marry one of them if you’re a successful producer, and catch their fancy. After all, there are numerous actress-producer couples dotted all over Bollywood. For instance, you’ve got Vidya Balan, Rani Mukherjee, Sonali Bendre, Sridevi, and Raveena Tandon. They all are or were married to film producers. If you just want to hang out with actresses, it’s not necessary that you must be a movie producer, of course. But no doubt, it gives you great opportunity to work with them, and see them on a more frequent basis etc etc. So, all things considered, not a shabby profession to choose if you want to hang out with the starlets.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why did Kat Dennings get blackballed from Hollywood?
Answer: Well, she actually didn’t get blackballed or blacklisted by Hollywood. Yes, she did kinda get dropped in the third Thor movie, but so too was Natalie Portman. And, she didn’t get blackballed by anyone, even after some of her private pictures were despicably leaked online. Question: Does only Australia have freshwater crocodiles?
Answer: Nope, most crocodile species are freshwater species, with the exception of Saltwater crocodiles or Salties. And, even Salties are found in several countries besides Australia. Of course, Australia also has Freshwater crocs or Johnstone’s crocodiles. Only those are found in Australia, but a majority of the crocodile species are freshwater ones, and found throughout the world, not just Australia. For instance, Muggers or Marsh Crocs are found In India and Iran, and even in Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Nepal. Gharials are found in India and Bangladesh. Both Muggers and Gharials are freshwater crocodiles. Then we have the infamous Nile crocs which are freshwater crocs, and found in loads of countries in Africa. Then, there’s the American crocodile, the Morelet crocodile, and the Orinoco crocodile, all of which can be found in different parts of North America and South America. All are freshwater crocodiles again. So, as you can see, the only freshwater croc species only found in Australia is the Johnstone’s crocodile. Loads of other countries have other kinds of freshwater crocodiles.

I mean, I am obviously biased because it happens to have Divya Bharti in it, and many other favorites of mine (Sunny Deol, Chunky Pandey, Gulshan Grover, etc.). Anyway, that’s pretty much the connection between Divya Bharti and the Pet Shop Boys. One of the iconic songs featuring her happens to be copied from a Pet Shop Boys’ hit. Here’s the links to both the songs - listen to them both to see the similarities. I like them both - even though Viju Shah copied it, he did so with enough of a change, that it works great! And, here’s the original PSB song. Listen to them both - which one do you prefer?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: I much prefer male superheroes over female superheroes. Does that make me sexist?
Answer: I don’t think that makes you sexist at all. You just identify better with male superheroes than their female counterparts. I like both male and female superheroes/comic characters, but I do find it a lot easier to identify with the male ones. For instance, I can imagine myself in Hellboy’s or John Constantine’s or Conan’s shoes a lot easier than I can in Red Sonja’s or Black Widow’s or Zatanna’s shoes. I imagine something like that is happening for you, which lead you to your marked preference. Also, you’ve maybe not read any of the good female superhero comics. Start reading some of the ones with Black Widow or Red Sonja or Wonder Woman, or Jessica Jones, and you’ll find that you will like female superheroes too, even if you still prefer male superheroes.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which actor should play Rockstar Kid Rock in a Hollywood movie?
Answer: I think the actor who would be perfect to play Kid Rock in a movie is Macaulay Culkin. Remember that phase of his from a few years back when he had everyone worried about him? Name: Aditya Simha

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which Indian Bollywood actor played a role in a movie that was similar to what Hollywood actor Neil Patrick Harris did? Do you think they did justice to the role and did you like the movie?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which Bollywood movie influenced you the most and why?
Answer: Hmm…this is an intriguing question to ponder on. I’ve seen so many movies throughout my life, that I bet my current personality has doubtless been influenced in many ways by several movies. So, in a sense, I’d say that there must be hundreds of movies that I’ve seen and liked that have influenced me, and had some effect on me as a person. However, I think you’re asking about the movies that have had the greatest impact on me, and changed me as a person, so to speak. So, I’ll mention a few here - 1. Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa (1993) This is my all-time favorite Shah Rukh Khan movie. This movie showcases pure innocence for me - the pangs of unrequited love, the natural goodness of people, the brilliantly essayed middle-class environs in the film, etc. All of these factors really spoke to me. About it changing me as a person though - I think one thing I picked up from this movie is that sometimes you just have to love people despite their flaws. And, sometimes you have to realize that you are surrounded by people who love you. In particular, the Woh To Hai Albela song emphasizes this beautiful message of KHKN. The message it showcases is that even if your loved one fails in something, you don’t just discount them as a person. So, I guess - another lesson I’ve picked up from this movie is if a loved one fails, you encourage them to try again. You must support them, and encourage them to try again and succeed. 2. Hare Rama Hare Krishna (1971) If anything is to be praised for me never having gotten into drug addiction, I suppose it must be Dev Anand’s Hare Rama Hare Krishna. By the time I saw this movie as a young kid, it was already 15+ years old, but even at that early age, I could recognize the myriad perils of drug addiction. I think this movie more than any other helped me form my negative attitude towards addictive drugs. I think Sanju will do something similar for anyone who watches it while young - it’ll crystallize that person’s negative attitude towards drugs. Of course, I should also thank the countless Bollywood action movies I’ve seen where the baddies are always selling drugs and get beaten up by the good guys (e.g. Jalwa, Tridev, Mohra, etc). But Hare Rama Hare Krishna is definitely the primary one. 3. Taare Zameen Par (2007) I really liked this movie of Aamir Khan’s when I first saw it. But now that I have young kids of my own, I really appreciate it a lot more. I truly appreciate the message that this movie brings forth. If you have kids, you jolly well support them even if they turn out to be “naughty kids” from a societal perspective. It’s very important to do that as parents or even just as adults. I think this movie has certainly had a subtle impact on my parenting style. Kids understand us a lot better than we understand them at times, y’know. 4. Ae Dil Hain Mushkil (2016) While ADHM hasn’t shaped my personality as much as the previous three films, it has given me the opportunity to recognize patterns in my own life. About ten years ago when I was a single college student, I had a rather traumatic (for me at least) case of unrequited love. Hell, when I saw ADHM, I could recognize my past self in the Ayan character. I wish ADHM had released back in 2008, it would have spared me much agony. But anyway, I mention this here because ADHM’s message is one that I think everyone should abide by. My advice to any friend/acquaintance suffering from a case of unrequited love is the same now - don’t be stupid like Ayan. Either accept that Alizeh will never be more than a friend to you, or else, walk the heck away. So, I guess while ADHM didn’t change me as a person, it gave me the opportunity to realize that I’d changed as a person by showing me my own past. Conclusion There are loads of movies which I think have influenced me as a person - but the four I’ve mentioned above are probably the ones that I can recognize as having had some impact on me as a person.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is there an actor/actress who never had a flop movie in their entire career?
Answer: Well from a Bollywood POV, the now disgraced godman Sant Ram Rahim Insan comes to mind. The rockstar baba made four movies, which were essentially a series of loosely connected sequels, with him involved in many aspects of the film (acting, singing, dancing, etc.). The Rockstar ex-baba and his adherents insisted that each movie was a brilliant box office success, and every single movie grossed over 100 crores each. If we buy their argument, then I guess the unholy Saint fits the bill. He gave 4 back-to-back hits until his career came to a grinding halt, due to the inconvenience caused by his going to prison. Of course, there is the niggling little fact that those box office numbers were never and have never been verified. But we live in a post-truth world, so we must accept the Sant’s word as 24- karat gold, even if it is 24-carrot fool’s gold!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is your opinion as former Pakistani cricketer Shoaib Akhtar claims marriage to Anushka Sharma harmed Virat Kohli's career?
Answer: I did not realize that Shoaib Akhtar had suddenly metamorphosed into Doctor Phil or Doctor Oz. I mean, after all, he’s busy dispensing unwanted and useless opinions. It is the height of ludicrousness to blame Anushka Sharma for having harmed Virat Kohli’s career. When all is said and done, Virat Kohli remains India’s most successful cricket captain. Shouldn’t Anushka get a bit of credit for that too? I find it appalling that anyone can think that a sport-person’s lull in their career is due to their spouse (usually wives get blamed). Poor Anushka keeps getting blamed every single time Virat has a dip in form. Highly ridiculous, and honestly, anyone who claims that ought to get their brains examined for tapeworms. Addendum… I was rather steamed initially, but now with a cooler head, I examined what Shoaib Akhtar really said. He hasn’t actually directly blamed Anushka Sharma (that idiotic headline is from the genius mind of whichever TOI writer wrote it). Shoaib Akhtar basically said that he would have wanted Virat to keep scoring centuries, and not get burdened by the captaincy. He then said that he wouldn’t have even married if he were in Virat’s place. So, he hasn’t exactly blamed Anushka directly, although, he has in an oblique fashion. Either way, it’s his opinion - I rather disagree with him. The fact remains that Virat is the most successful Indian cricket captain of all time. And, if you’re going to blame Anushka for his failures, then you bloody well need to give her credit for his successes.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What is the meaning of the popular song ‘Oo Antava’ from the movie ‘Pushpa’ that features famous actors Allu Arjun and Samantha? Why has it been dubbed into so many other Indian regional languages? Do you like the song?
Answer: That particular song is essentially a raunchy item song. It is being marketed and talked about like it’s some sort of feminist empowering song with a social message. However, dressing up a crocodile in a Chanel outfit does not change the fact that we’re still looking at a crocodile. The song is essentially about how girls and women are ogled and catcalled at by boys and men throughout their lives, and how no matter how the girl or woman is, there will be some lad or man waiting in the wings, ready to shower his (un)wanted attentions on that girl or woman. Why was it dubbed into so many languages? That was more because the movie was dubbed into many languages, so they went the whole hog, and got it sung in other languages too. Do I like the song? It’s alright - I don’t love it but I don’t hate it either. The makers shouldn’t have tried to justify it by calling it a “social message song”. It’s a raunchy item song, and no amount of dressing it up is going to make it a “social message song”. They ought to have been honest and said, “Yeah, it’s an item song! Don’t like it? Then, don’t watch it! But we know, you will!”

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Does the Bollywood cinema have any films inspired by the Italian sword and sandals pictures (also known as peplum) from the 1960s?
Answer: I can’t think of any Bollywood movies that could be said to be wholly inspired by the Italian sword and sandal peplum flicks of the 60s. The Greco-Roman type of epics probably wouldn’t translate well in a Hindi film, at least not directly. I can think of one film though, Dharam Veer. The film is more or less an Indian epic type of story, but the main lead Dharmendra does sport a peplum inspired outfit in the film. It’s a good flick even if it’s a bit melodramatic in spots. But it’s not really the same as an Italian peplum flick.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Apart from ratatouille, what dishes have great names?
Answer: My favorite name of a dish is Benaami Kheer. So, kheer essentially is a porridge/pudding kind of Indian dish, and typically made with milk and rice or milk and vermicelli. The Benaami refers to unknown or nameless - that’s because the chefs who created this first had a secret unexpected ingredient in it, which they initially refused to disclose. That delightful ingredient happens to be garlic. Yes, garlic! Ever wondered if you could use garlic in a sweet dish/dessert? Now you don’t have to wonder anymore. Simply try making this dish in your own kitchen, and if it works out alright - shock your dining guests (not an anaphylactic shock, of course!) Keep them guessing! The image and delicious recipe can be found on Chef Reetu Uday Kugaji’s website. Her website is her complete name followed by a dot com.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why did the actor Dhanush get divorced in 2022?
Answer: We don’t know why Dhanush and Aishwaryaa divorced. Neither of them has been forthcoming about the exact reasons as to why. And most likely, neither of them will ever reveal the exact set of reasons either. We will only know as much as that hollow joint statement which all celebrities seem to release after their divorce (e.g. we love each other but choose to go our separate parts) reveals. I did come across two gossipy articles, one of which is by Subhash K. Jha, who has supposedly talked with some “major Tamil actor”, who revealed to Jha, that the fault lay entirely with Dhanush. He hints at rumored infidelity as the cause of it. Another gossipy article suggests that Dhanush’s workaholic tendencies laid the foundation to their marriage’s crumbling. I don’t know which account is accurate, but I would suspect that there are probably elements of truth to all of the speculative articles. Well, except for their first soppy joint statement- that one was crafted by some PR person who doesn’t want excessive brand damage.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why is Katrina Kaif so unattractive?
Answer: She is not unattractive to me (and many other people as well). In fact, we would all agree that Katrina Kaif is rather attractive. Now, she may not be for you, and that’s quite alright. Name: Aditya Simha
Question: In a 𝑁𝑒𝑤 𝑌𝑜𝑟𝑘 𝑇𝑖𝑚𝑒𝑠 editorial, Thomas Friedman is promoting a Biden-Liz Cheney ticket for 2024. What are your thoughts?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Does fruit belong in savoury dishes? If so, could you provide us with a convincing recipe/photo?
Answer: Oh absolutely! Although, I must say that unripe fruit tends to go better in savory dishes than ripe fruit, because ripe fruit tends to make the savory dish somewhat unduly sweet. Having said that, here are some of my favorite savory dishes all made from fruit, and indeed the fruit is indispensable in these dishes. 1. Jackfruit - Dishes made from unripe/raw jackfruit are among my most favorite dishes of all. Check out the many Biryanis, Currys, Stir-Fry dishes, etc., that you can make with jackfruit. This image and the delicious recipe involved can be found at Archana’s Kitchen’s blog. 2. Plantains - Stir-fry, deep-fry, or just boil/saute them. One of my favorite kababs of all are Phaldhaari kababs, which are made with boiled plantain dough, which is then grilled or fried. The image and delicious recipe can be found at cookpad.com, and the creator is a certain Archana Bhargava. 3. Lemon/Lime - Can’t go wrong with either Lemon/Lime Rice or Lemon/Lime Rasam. Both dishes are quite amazing! The image and delicious recipe are from Geetha’s Flavours Treat blog. 4. Breadfruit - This is sorta similar to jackfruit, but I personally find jackfruit to be tastier. Still, you can make a decent curry or stir-fry with breadfruit. Or just roast it, and add some spicy seasoning on it, to mask the otherwise blandly sweet breadfruit. The image and delicious recipe are from Suji’s Cooking blog. 5. Mango - There is a dish called mango pappu/daal, which combines the flavors of mango with lentils. Similarly, one can make a dish called mango chitranna, which is basically lemon rice with mango flavoring. This image and the delicious recipe involved can be found at Vysyas’ recipes blog. And, of course, tomatoes. Nothing better than tomatoes in making savory dishes- both ripe and unripe tomatoes go smashingly well in all savory dishes. I trust these five examples will get anyone reading to give the dishes a try. They are well worth the effort.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which actor portrayed the Devil best, and in what movie/TV show?
Answer: I scrolled through the other answers expecting to see my pick already there, but he doesn’t seem to be. So, here is my pick - Ewan McGregor for his brilliant performance in Last Days in the Desert. He plays both Jesus as well as Satan, and plays them both in exemplary fashion. The movie isn’t that well known, and indeed, I suspect only about 67 people across the world have seen it thus far. But I hope that number rises, because Ewan McGregor is fantastic in the movie. Do watch it, but do pay attention to the film - it’s not one of those films where you can scroll through your phone, while still enjoying what’s happening on screen.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Who killed Madhuri Dixit?
Answer: What a nonsensical question, and that one anon answer skates on the scratchy thin line between insanity and mad parody. Madhuri Dixit is very much alive, and doing absolutely fine.
